body.input: And his conclusion from that was that

body.input: if some alien species developed higher intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: they would at least have arithmetic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: They would at least have what the simplest computer would do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And in fact, he didn't know that at the time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: but the core principles of natural language

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: are based on operations which yield something

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: like arithmetic in the limiting case and the minimal case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So it's conceivable that a mode of communication

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: could be established based on the core properties

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: of human language and the core properties of arithmetic,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: which maybe are universally shared.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So it's conceivable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: What is the structure of that language,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: of language as an internal system inside our mind

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: versus an external system as it's expressed?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's not an alternative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's two different concepts of language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's a simple fact that there's something about you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: a trait of yours, part of the organism you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that determines that you're talking English

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and not Tagalog, let's say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So there is an inner system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It determines the sound and meaning

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: of the infinite number of expressions of your language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's localized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's not in your foot, obviously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's in your brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: If you look more closely,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: it's in specific configurations of your brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And that's essentially like the internal structure

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: of your laptop, whatever programs it has are in there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Now, one of the things you can do with language,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: it's a marginal thing, in fact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: is use it to externalize what's in your head.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Actually, most of your use of language

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: is thought, internal thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But you can do what you and I are now doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: We can externalize it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Well, the set of things that we're externalizing

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: are an external system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: They're noises in the atmosphere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And you can call that language

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: in some other sense of the word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But it's not a set of alternatives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: These are just different concepts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So how deep do the roots of language go in our brain?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Our mind, is it yet another feature like vision,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: or is it something more fundamental

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: from which everything else springs in the human mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Well, in a way, it's like vision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: There's something about our genetic endowment

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that determines that we have a mammalian

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: rather than an insect visual system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And there's something in our genetic endowment

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that determines that we have a human language faculty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: No other organism has anything remotely similar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So in that sense, it's internal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Now, there is a long tradition,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: which I think is valid going back centuries

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: to the early scientific revolution, at least,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that holds that language is the sort of the core

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: of human cognitive nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's the source.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's the mode for constructing thoughts and expressing them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: That is what forms thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And it's got fundamental creative capacities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's free, independent, unbounded, and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And undoubtedly, I think the basis

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: for our creative capacities and the other remarkable

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: human capacities that lead to the unique achievements

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and not so great achievements of the species.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: The capacity to think and reason,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: do you think that's deeply linked with language?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Do you think the way the internal language system

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: is essentially the mechanism

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: by which we also reason internally?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It is undoubtedly the mechanism by which we reason.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: There may also be other, there are undoubtedly

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: other faculties involved in reasoning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: We have a kind of scientific faculty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Nobody knows what it is, but whatever it is

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that enables us to pursue certain lines of endeavor

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and inquiry and to decide what makes sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and doesn't make sense and to achieve

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: certain degree of understanding of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: That uses language, but goes beyond it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Just as using our capacity for arithmetic

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: is not the same as having the capacity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: The idea of capacity, our biology, evolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: you've talked about it defining essentially our capacity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: our limit and our scope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Can you try to define what limit and scope are?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And the bigger question, do you think it's possible

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: to find the limit of human cognition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Well, that's an interesting question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's commonly believed, most scientists believe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that human intelligence can answer

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: any question in principle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: I think that's a very strange belief.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: If we're biological organisms,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: which are not angels, then our capacities

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: ought to have scope and limits, which are interrelated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Can you define those two terms?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Well, let's take a concrete example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Your genetic endowment determines

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that you can have a male-in-visual system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: arms and legs and so on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: but it can therefore become a rich, complex organism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But if you look at that same genetic endowment,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: it prevents you from developing in other directions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: There's no kind of experience which would yield

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: the embryo to develop an insect-visual system

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: or to develop wings instead of arms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So the very endowment that confers richness and complexity

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: also sets bounds on what can be attained.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Now, I assume that our cognitive capacities

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: are part of the organic world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: therefore they should have the same properties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: If they had no built-in capacity

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: to develop a rich and complex structure,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: we would understand nothing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Just as if your genetic endowment

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: did not compel you to develop arms and legs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: you would just be some kind of random amoeboid creature

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: with no structure at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So I think it's plausible to assume that there are limits,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and I think we even have some evidence as to what they are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So for example, there's a classic moment

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: in the history of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: At the time of Newton, there was a,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: from Galileo to Newton, modern science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: developed on a fundamental assumption,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: which Newton also accepted,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: namely that the world, the entire universe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: is a mechanical object.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And by mechanical, they meant something

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: like the kinds of artifacts that were being developed

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: by skilled artisans all over Europe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: gears, levers, and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And their belief was, well, the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: is just a more complex variant of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Newton, to his astonishment and distress,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: proved that there are no machines,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that there's interaction without contact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: His contemporaries like Leibniz and Huygens

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: just dismissed this as returning to the mysticism

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: of the neoscholastics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And Newton agreed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: He said, it is totally absurd.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: No person of any scientific intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: could ever accept this for a moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: In fact, he spent the rest of his life

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: trying to get around it somehow,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: as did many other scientists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: That was the very criterion of intelligibility

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: for, say, Galileo or Newton.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Theory did not produce an intelligible world

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: unless you could duplicate it in a machine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: He said, you can't, there are no machines.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And finally, after a long struggle, took a long time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: scientists just accepted this as common sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But that's a significant moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: That means they abandoned the search

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: for an intelligible world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And the great philosophers of the time

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: understood that very well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So, for example, David Hume, in his Encomium to Newton,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: wrote that, who was the greatest thinker ever,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: He said that he unveiled many of the secrets of nature,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: but by showing the imperfections

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: of the mechanical philosophy, mechanical science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: he left us with, he showed that there are mysteries

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: which ever will remain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And science just changed its goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It abandoned the mysteries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It can't solve it, we'll put it aside.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: We only look for intelligible theories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Newton's theories were intelligible,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: it's just what they described wasn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Well, Locke said the same thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: I think they're basically right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And if so, that showed something about the limits

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: of human cognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: We cannot attain the goal of understanding the world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: of finding an intelligible world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: This mechanical philosophy, Galileo to Newton,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: there's a good case that can be made

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that that's our instinctive conception of how things work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So if, say, infants are tested with things that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: if this moves, then this moves,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: they kind of invent something that must be invisible,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that's in between them, that's making them move, and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Yeah, we like physical contact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Something about our brain seeks...

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Makes us want a world like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Just like it wants a world that has regular geometric figures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So, for example, Descartes pointed this out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that if you have an infant who's never seen a triangle before,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and you draw a triangle,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: the infant will see a distorted triangle,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: not whatever crazy figure it actually is, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: three lines not coming quite together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: or one of them a little bit curved, and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: We just impose a conception of the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: in terms of a geometric, perfect geometric object.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's now been shown that goes way beyond that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that if you show on a tachistoscope,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: let's say, a couple of lights shining,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: you do it three or four times in a row,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: what people actually see is a rigid object in motion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: not whatever's there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: That's... We all know that from a television set, basically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So that gives us hints of potential limits to our cognition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: I think it does, but it's a very contested view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: If you do a poll among scientists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: it's impossible we can understand anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Let me ask and give me a chance with this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So I just spent a day at a company called Neuralink,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and what they do is try to design what's called

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: the brain-machine-brain-computer interface.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So they try to do thousands of readings in the brain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: be able to read what the neurons are firing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and then stimulate back, so two-way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Do you think their dream is to expand the capacity of the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: to attain information, sort of increase the bandwidth

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: to which we can search Google, kind of thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Do you think our cognitive capacity might be expanded,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: our linguistic capacity, our ability to reason

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: might be expanded by adding a machine into the picture?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It can be expanded in a certain sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: but a sense that was known thousands of years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: A book expands your cognitive capacity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Okay, so this could expand it, too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But it's not a fundamental expansion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's not totally new things could be understood.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Well, nothing that goes beyond our native cognitive capacities,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: just like you can't turn the visual system into an insect system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Well, I mean, the thought is perhaps you can't directly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: but you can map.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: You couldn't, but we already know that without this experiment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: You could map what a bee sees and present it in a form

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: so that we could follow it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: In fact, every bee scientist does that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But you don't think there's something greater than bees

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that we can map and then all of a sudden discover something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: be able to understand a quantum world, quantum mechanics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: be able to start to be able to make sense?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Students at MIT study and understand quantum mechanics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But they always reduce it to the infant, the physical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: I mean, they don't really understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Oh, you don't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: There's things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: That may be another area where there's just a limit to understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: We understand the theories, but the world that it describes

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: doesn't make any sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So, you know, the experiment, Schrodinger's cat, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: can understand the theory, but as Schrodinger pointed out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: it's an unintelligible world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: One of the reasons why Einstein was always very skeptical

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: about quantum theory, he described himself as a classical realist

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: once then, in one's intelligibility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: He has something in common with infants in that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So, back to linguistics, if you could humor me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: what are the most beautiful or fascinating aspects of language

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: or ideas in linguistics or cognitive science that you've seen

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: in a lifetime of studying language and studying the human mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Well, I think the deepest property of language

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and puzzling property that's been discovered is

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: what is sometimes called structure dependence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: We now understand it pretty well, but it was puzzling for a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: I'll give you a concrete example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Suppose you say the guy who fixed the car carefully packed his tools.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's ambiguous.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: He could fix the car carefully or carefully pack his tools.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Suppose you put carefully in front.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Carefully the guy who fixed the car packed his tools.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Then it's carefully packed, not carefully fixed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And in fact, you do that even if it makes no sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So suppose you say carefully the guy who fixed the car is tall.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: You have to interpret it as carefully he's tall,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: even though that doesn't make any sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And notice that that's a very puzzling fact

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: because you're relating carefully not to the linearly closest verb,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: but to the linearly more remote verb.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Linear closeness is an easy computation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: but here you're doing what looks like a more complex computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: You're doing something that's taking you essentially to the more remote thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: If you look at the actual structure of the sentence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: where the phrases are and so on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: turns out you're picking out the structurally closest thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: but the linearly more remote thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But notice that what's linear is 100% of what you hear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: You never hear structure. You can't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So what you're doing is, and instantly this is universal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: all constructions, all languages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And what we're compelled to do is carry out what looks like

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: the more complex computation on material that we never hear,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and we ignore 100% of what we hear and the simplest computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: By now there's even a neural basis for this that's somewhat understood,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and there's good theories by now that explain why it's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: That's a deep insight into the surprising nature of language with many consequences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Let me ask you about a field of machine learning, deep learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: There's been a lot of progress in neural network-based machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: in the recent decade.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Of course, neural network research goes back many decades.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: What do you think are the limits of deep learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: of neural network-based machine learning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Well, to give a real answer to that, you'd have to understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: the exact processes that are taking place, and those are pretty opaque.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So it's pretty hard to prove a theorem about what can be done and what can't be done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But I think it's reasonably clear.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: I mean, putting technicalities aside, what deep learning is doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: is taking huge numbers of examples and finding some patterns.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Okay, that could be interesting in some areas it is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: but we have to ask here a certain question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Is it engineering or is it science?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Engineering in the sense of just trying to build something that's useful,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: or science in the sense that it's trying to understand something

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: about elements of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So it takes a Google parser.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: We can ask that question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Is it useful? Yeah, it's pretty useful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: I use a Google translator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So on engineering grounds, it's kind of worth having, like a bulldozer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Does it tell you anything about human language?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Zero. Nothing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And in fact, it's very striking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: From the very beginning, it's just totally remote from science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So what is a Google parser doing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's taking an enormous text, let's say the Wall Street Journal corpus,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and asking how close can we come to getting the right description

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: of every sentence in the corpus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Well, every sentence in the corpus is essentially an experiment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Each sentence that you produce is an experiment which says,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: am I a grammatical sentence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: The answer is usually yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So most of the stuff in the corpus is grammatical sentences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But now ask yourself, is there any science which takes random experiments

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: which are carried out for no reason whatsoever

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and tries to find out something from them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Like if you're, say, a chemistry PhD student, you want to get a thesis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Can you say, well, I'm just going to mix a lot of things together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: no purpose, and maybe I'll find something?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: You'd be laughed out of the department.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But science tries to find critical experiments,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: ones that answer some theoretical question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It doesn't care about coverage of millions of experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So it just begins by being very remote from science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: and it continues like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So the usual question that's asked about, say, a Google parser is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: how well does it do, or some parser, how well does it do on a corpus?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But there's another question that's never asked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: How well does it do on something that violates all the rules of language?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So, for example, take the structured dependence case that I mentioned.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Suppose there was a language in which you used linear proximity

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: as the mode of interpretation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: These deep learning would work very easily on that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: in fact, much more easily than an actual language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Is that a success? No, that's a failure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: From a scientific point of view, it's a failure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It shows that we're not discovering the nature of the system at all,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: because it does just as well or even better on things

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that violate the structure of the system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And it goes on from there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's not an argument against doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It is useful to have devices like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So, yes, neural networks are kind of approximators that look...

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: There's echoes of the behavioral debates, right, behavioralism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: More than echoes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Many of the people in deep learning say they've vindicated...

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Terry Sanyosky, for example, in his recent books says,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: this vindicates skinerian behaviors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It doesn't have anything to do with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Yes, but I think there's something actually fundamentally different

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: when the data set is huge, but your point is extremely well taken.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But do you think we can learn, approximate that interesting complex

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: structure of language with neural networks that will somehow help us

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: understand the science?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: I mean, you find patterns that you hadn't noticed, let's say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Could be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: In fact, it's very much like a kind of linguistics that's done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: What's called corpus linguistics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: When you... suppose you have some language where all the speakers have died out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: but you have records.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So you just look at the records and see what you can figure out from that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's much better to have actual speakers where you can do critical experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But if they're all dead, you can't do them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So you have to try to see what you can find out from just looking at the data

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: that's around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: You can learn things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And actually paleoanthropology is very much like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: You can't do a critical experiment on what happened two million years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So you're kind of forced just to take what data's around and see what you can

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: figure out from it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's a serious study.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So let me venture into another whole body of work and philosophical question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: You've said that evil in society arises from institutions, not inherently from

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: our nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Do you think most human beings are good?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: They have good intent?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Or do most have the capacity for intentional evil that depends on their bringing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: depends on their environment, on context?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: I wouldn't say that they don't arise from our nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Anything we do arises from our nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And the fact that we have certain institutions, not others, is one mode in

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: which human nature has expressed itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But as far as we know, human nature could yield many different kinds of

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: institutions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: The particular ones that have developed have to do with historical contingency,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: who conquered whom and that sort of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: They're not rooted in our nature in the sense that they're essential to our

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So it's commonly argued that these days that something like market systems is

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: just part of our nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But we know from a huge amount of evidence that that's not true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: There's all kinds of other structures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's a particular fact about a moment of modern history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Others have argued that the roots of classical liberalism actually argue that

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: what's called sometimes an instinct for freedom, an instinct to be free of

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: domination by illegitimate authority is the core of our nature.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: That would be the opposite of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And we don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: We just know that human nature can accommodate both kinds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: If you look back at your life, is there a moment in your intellectual life or

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: life in general that jumps from memory that brought you happiness that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: would love to relive again?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Falling in love, having children.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: What about, so you have put forward into the world a lot of incredible ideas in

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: linguistics, in cognitive science, in terms of ideas that just excites you when

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: they first came to you, that you would love to relive those moments?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Well, I mean, when you make a discovery about something that's exciting, like

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: say even the observation of structure dependence and on from that the

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: explanation for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But the major things just seem like common sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So if you go back to take your question about external and internal language,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: you go back to say the 1950s, almost entirely language is regarded an

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: external object, something outside the mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It just seemed obvious that that can't be true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Like I said, there's something about you that determines you're talking

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: English, not Swahili or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But that's not really a discovery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: That's just an observation that's transparent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: You might say it's kind of like the 17th century, the beginnings of modern

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: science, 17th century.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: They came from being willing to be puzzled about things that seemed obvious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So it seems obvious that a heavy ball of lead will fall faster than a light

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: ball of lead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But Galileo was not impressed by the fact that it seemed obvious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So he wanted to know if it's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: They carried out experiments, actually thought experiments, never actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: carried them out, which would that can't be true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And out of things like that, observations of that kind, why does a ball fall to

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: ground instead of rising, let's say, seems obvious until you start thinking

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Why does steam rise?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And I think the beginnings of modern linguistics roughly in the 50s are kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: of like that, just being willing to be puzzled about phenomena that looked

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: from some point of view obvious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: For example, a kind of doctrine, almost official doctrine of structural

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: linguistics in the 50s was that languages can differ from one another in

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: arbitrary ways and each one has to be studied on its own without any

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: presuppositions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: In fact, there were similar views among biologists about the nature of

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: organisms, that each one is so different when you look at them that almost

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: anything, you could be almost anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Well, in both domains it's been learned that that's very far from true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: There are very narrow constraints on what could be an organism or what could

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: be a language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: But these are, you know, that's just the nature of inquiry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Science in general, yeah, inquiry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: So one of the peculiar things about us human beings is our mortality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Ernest Becker explored it in general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Do you ponder the value of mortality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Do you think about your own mortality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: I used to when I was about 12 years old.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: I wondered, I didn't care much about my own mortality, but I was worried about

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: the fact that if my consciousness disappeared, would the entire universe

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: disappear?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: That was frightening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Did you ever find an answer to that question?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: No.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53
