body.input: Nobody's ever found an answer, but I stopped being bothered by it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It's kind of like Woody Allen in one of his films, you may recall.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: He starts, he goes to a shrink when he's a child and the shrink asks him,

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: what's your problem?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: He says, I just learned that the universe is expanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: I can't handle that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: And then another absurd question is, what do you think is the meaning of our

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: existence here, our life on earth, our brief little moment in time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: That's something we answer by our own activities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: There's no general answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: We determine what the meaning of it is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: The action determining the meaning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Meaning in the sense of significance, not meaning in the sense that chair

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: means this, you know, but the significance of your life is something

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: you create.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: No, thank you so much for talking today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: It was a huge honor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Chomsky: Language, Cognition, and Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #53

body.input: Thank you so much.

body.input: And now, here's my conversation with Stephen Kotkin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Do all human beings crave power?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: No.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Human beings crave security, they crave love,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: they crave adventure, they crave power, but not equally.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Some human beings nevertheless do crave power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: For sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Where is that deeply in the psychology of people?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Is it something you're born with?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Is it something you develop?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Some people crave a position of leadership

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: or of standing out, of being recognized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And that could be starting out in the school years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: on the schoolyard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It could be within their own family,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: not just in their peer group.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Those kind of people we often see

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: craving leadership positions from a young age

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: often end up in positions of power,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but they can be varied positions of power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You can have power in an institution

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: where your power is purposefully limited.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: For example, there's a board or a consultative body

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: or a separation of powers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Not everyone craves power whereby they're the sole power

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: or they're their unconstrained power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: That's a little bit less usual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: We may think that everybody does, but not everybody does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Those people who do crave that kind of power,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: unconstrained the ability to decide as much as life or death

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: of other people, those people are not everyday people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: They're not the people you encounter in your daily life

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: for the most part.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Those are extraordinary people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Most of them don't have the opportunity to live that dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Very few of them, in fact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: end up with the opportunity to live that dream.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So percentage-wise, in your sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: if we think of George Washington, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: would most people, given the choice of absolute power

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: over a country versus maybe the capped power

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that the United States presidential role,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: at least at the founding of the country, represented,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: what do you think most people would choose?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Well, Washington was in a position

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: to exercise far greater power than he did.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And in fact, he didn't take that option.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He was more interested in seeing institutionalization

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: of seeing the country develop strong institutions

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: rather than an individual leader like himself

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: have excess power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So that's very important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So like I said, not everyone craves unconstrained power,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: even if they're very ambitious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And of course, Washington was very ambitious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He was a successful general before he was a president.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So that clearly comes from the influences on your life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: where you grow up, how you grow up, how you raised,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: what kind of values are imparted to you along the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You can understand power as the ability to share,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: or you can understand,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: or the ability to advance something for the collective

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: in a collective process, not an individual process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So power comes in many different varieties,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and ambition doesn't always equate to despotic power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Despotic power is something different

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: from ordinary institutional power that we see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The president of MIT does not have unconstrained power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The president of MIT rightly must consult

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: with other members of the administration,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: with the faculty members,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: to a certain extent with the student body,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and certainly with the trustees of MIT.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Those constraints make the institution strong and enduring

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and make the decisions better than they would be

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: if he had unconstrained power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But you can't say that the president is not ambitious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Of course the president is ambitious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: We worry about unconstrained power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: We worry about executive authority that's not limited.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: That's the definition of authoritarianism or tyranny.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Unlimited or barely limited executive authority.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Executive authority is necessary

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: to carry out many functions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: We all understand that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: That's why MIT has an executive, has a president.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But unlimited or largely unconstrained executive power

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: is detrimental to even the person who exercises that power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So what do you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It's an interesting notion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: We kind of take it for granted

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that constraints on executive power is a good thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But why is that necessarily true?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So what is it about absolute power

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that does something bad to the human mind?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So the popular saying of absolute power corrupts absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Is that the case?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: That the power in itself is the thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that corrupts the mind in some kind of way

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: where it leads to a bad leadership over time?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: People make more mistakes when they're not challenged,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: when they don't have to explain things

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and get others to vote and go along with it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: when they can make a decision

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: without anybody being able to block their decision

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: or to have input necessarily on their decision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You're more prone to mistakes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You're more prone to extremism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: There's a temptation there.

body.input: Russia has an election during the war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: a free and fair election for the most part,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: despite the war, at the end of 1917,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: in December 1917,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and three-quarters plus of the country votes socialist

body.input: in some form or another.

body.input: So the battle was over the definition of socialism

body.input: and who had the right to participate in defining socialism,

body.input: not only what it would be,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but who had the right to decide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So there's a coup by Lenin's group known as the Bolsheviks

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: against all the other socialists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so Lenin declares a seizure of power

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: whereby the old government has failed,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: people's power, the councils, known as the Soviets,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: are going to take their place,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and Lenin seizes power in the name of the Soviets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So it's a coup against the left, against the rest of the left,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: not against the provisional government

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that has replaced the Tsar, which has already failed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so Stalin is able to come to power, along with Lenin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: in this crazy seizure of power on the left

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: against the rest of the left in October 1917,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: which we know is the October Revolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and I call the October Coup, as many other historians call.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The October Revolution happened after the seizure of power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: What's interesting about this episode

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: is that the leftists who seize power

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: in the name of the Soviets, in the name of the masses,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: in the name of people's power,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: they retain their hold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Many times in history there's a seizure of power by the left,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and they fail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: They collapse, they're cleaned out by an army

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: or what we call forces of order,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: by counter-revolutionary forces.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Lenin's revolution, Lenin's coup,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: is successful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It is able to hold power, not just seize power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: They win a civil war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and they're entrenched in the heart of the country

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: already by 1921.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Stalin is part of that group.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Lenin needs somebody to run this new regime

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: in the kind of nitty-gritty way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Lenin is the leader, the undisputed leader

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: in the Bolshevik party,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: which changes their name to Communists in 1918.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He makes Stalin

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: the general secretary of the Communist party.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He creates a new position,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: which hadn't existed before,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: a kind of day-to-day political manager,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: a right-hand man.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Not because Lenin is looking to replace himself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: he's looking to institutionalize a helpmate, a right-hand man.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He does this in the spring of 1922.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Stalin is named to this position,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: which Lenin has created expressly for Stalin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So there's been a coup on the left,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: whereby the Bolsheviks, who become Communists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: have seized power against the rest of the Socialists

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and the Anarchists and the entire left.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And then there's an institutionalization

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: of a position known as general secretary

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: of the Communist party,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: right-hand man of Lenin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Less than six weeks after Lenin has created this position

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and installed Stalin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Lenin has a stroke,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: a major stroke,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and never really returns as a full actor

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: to power before he dies of a fourth stroke

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: in January 1924.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So a position is created for Stalin

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: to run things on Lenin's behalf,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and then Lenin has a stroke.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so Stalin now has this new position general secretary,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but he's the right hand of a person

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: who's no longer exercising day-to-day control over affairs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Stalin then uses this new position

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: to create a personal dictatorship

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: inside the Bolshevik dictatorship,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: which is the remarkable story I tried to tell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So is there anything nefarious

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: about any of what you just described?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So it seems conveniently

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that the position is created just for Stalin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: There was a few other brilliant people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: arguably more brilliant than Stalin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: in the vicinity of Lenin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Why was Stalin chosen?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Why did Lenin all of a sudden fall ill?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It's perhaps a conspiratorial question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but is there anything nefarious

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: about any of this historical trajectory to power

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that Stalin took in creating the personal dictatorship?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So history is full of contingency and surprise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: After something happens,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: we all think it's inevitable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It had to happen that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Everything was leading up to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So Hitler seizes power in Germany in 1933,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and the Nazi regime gets institutionalized

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: by several of his moves after being named chancellor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so all German history becomes a story

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: of the Nazi rise to power, Hitler's rise to power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Every trend, tendency is bent into that outcome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Things which don't seem related to that outcome

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: all of a sudden get bent in that direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And other trends that were going on

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: are no longer examined

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: because they didn't lead to that outcome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But Hitler's becoming chancellor of Germany in 1933

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: was not inevitable, it was contingent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He was offered the position by the traditional conservatives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He's part of the radical right,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and the traditional right named him chancellor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The Nazi party never outright won an election

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that was free and fair before Hitler came to power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And in fact, its votes on the eve of Hitler becoming chancellor

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: declined relative to the previous election.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So there's contingency in history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and so Lenin's illness, his stroke,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: the neurological and blood problems that he had

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: were not a structure in history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: In other words, if Lenin had been a healthier figure,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Stalin might never have become the Stalin that we know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: That's not to say that all history is accidental,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: just that we need to relate the larger structural factors

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: to the contingent factors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Why did Lenin pick Stalin?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Well, Stalin was a very effective organizer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and the position was an organizational position.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Stalin could get things done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He would carry out assignments, no matter how difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He wouldn't complain that it was hard work or too much work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He wouldn't go off womanizing and drinking

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and ignore his responsibilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Lenin chose Stalin, among other options,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: because he thought Stalin was the better option.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Once again, he wasn't choosing his successor

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: because he didn't know he was going to have this stroke.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Lenin had some serious illnesses,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but he had never had a major stroke before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So the choice was made based upon Stalin's organizational skills

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and promise against the others who were in the regime.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Now, they can seem more brilliant than Stalin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but he was more effective,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and I'm not sure they were very brilliant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Well, he was exceptionally competent actually at the tasks

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: for running a government, the executive branch, right,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: of a dictator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Yes, he turned out to be very adept at being a dictator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so if he had been chosen by Lenin and had not been very good,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: he would have been pushed aside by others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You can get a position by accident.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You can be named because you're someone's friend

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: or someone's relative, but to hold that position,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: to hold that position in difficult circumstances,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and then to build effectively a superpower on all that bloodshed, right,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: you have to be skilled in some way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It can't be just the accident that brings you to power

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: because if accident brings you to power, it won't last.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Just like we discovered with Putin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: he had some qualities that we didn't foresee at the beginning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and he's been able to hold power, not just be named into it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Now, Putin and Stalin are very different people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: These are very different regimes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I wouldn't put them in the same sentence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: My point is not that one resembles the other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: My point is that when people come to power for contingent reasons,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: they don't stay in power unless they're able to manage it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And Stalin was able to build a personal dictatorship inside that dictatorship.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He was cunning. He was ruthless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And he was a workaholic. He was very diligent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He had a phenomenal memory,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and so he could remember people's names and faces and events,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and this was very advantageous for him as he built the machine

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that became the Soviet state and bureaucracy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: One of the things maybe you can correct me if I'm wrong,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: you've made me realize is this wasn't some kind of manipulative personality

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: trying to gain more power solely,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: like kind of an evil picture of a person,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but he truly believed in communism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: As far as I can understand, again, you can correct me if I'm wrong,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but he wanted to build a better world

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: by having infused communism into the country,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: perhaps into the whole world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So maybe my question is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: what role does communism as an idea, as an ideology play in all of this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: in his rise to power, in the people of the time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: in the Russian people, actually just the whole 20th century?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You're right. Stalin was a true believer, and this is very important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He was also hungry for power and for personal power,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but just as you said, not for power's sake, not only for power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He was interested in enacting communism in reality

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and also in building a powerful state.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He was a statist, a traditional Russian statist in the imperial sense,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and this won him a lot of followers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The fact that they knew he was a hardcore true believing communist

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: won him a lot of followers among the communists,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and the fact that he was a hardcore defender of Russian state interests,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: now in the Soviet guise, also won him a lot of followers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Sometimes those groups overlapped, the communists and the Russian patriots,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and sometimes they were completely different groups,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but both of them shared an admiration for Stalin's dedication to those goals

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and his abilities to enact them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So it's very important to understand that however thirsty he was for power,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and he was very thirsty for power, that he was also driven by ideals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Now, I don't necessarily think that everyone around Stalin shared those ideals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: We have to be careful not to make everybody into a communist true believer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: not to make everybody into a great statist Russian patriot,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but they were widespread and powerful attractions for a lot of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so Stalin's ability to communicate to people that he was dedicated to those pursuits

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and his ability to drive towards them were part of his appeal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: However, he also resorted to manipulation, he also resorted to violence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: he lied, he spoke out of all sides of his mouth, he slandered other people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: he sabotaged potential rivals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: he used every underhanded method and then some in order to build his personal dictatorship.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Now, he justified this, as you said, by appeals to communism and to Soviet power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: To himself as well, too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: To himself and to others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so he justified it in his own mind and to others,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but certainly any means were acceptable to him to achieve these ends.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And he identified his personal power with communism and with Russian glory in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So he felt that he was the only one who could be trusted,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: who could be relied upon to build these things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Now, we put ourselves back in that time period.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The Great Depression was a very difficult time for the capitalist system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: There was mass unemployment, a lot of hardship,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: fascism, Nazism, Imperial Japan.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: There were a lot of associations that were negative with the kind of capitalist system

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that was not 100%, not a monolith, but had a lot of authoritarian incarnations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: There was imperialism, colonies that even the democratic rule of law capitalist states

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: had non-democratic, non-rule of law colonies under their rule.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So the image and reality of capitalism during that time period

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: between World War I and World War II was very different from how it would become later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so in that time period, in that interwar conjuncture after World War I, before World War II,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: communism held some appeal inside the Soviet Union for sure,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but even outside the Soviet Union because the image and reality of capitalism disappointed many people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Now, in the end, communism was significantly worse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Many more victims and the system, of course, would eventually implode.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But nonetheless, there were real problems that communism tried to address.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It didn't solve those problems. It was not a solution, but it didn't come out of nowhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It came out of the context of that interwar period.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so Stalin's rule, some people saw it as potentially a better option

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: than imperialism, fascism, and Great Depression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Having said that, they were wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It turned out that Stalin wasn't a better alternative to markets and private property and rule of law and democracy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: However, that didn't become clearer to people until after World War II,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: after Nazism had been defeated, Imperial Japan had been defeated,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: fascist Italy had been defeated, and decolonization had happened around the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And there was a middle class economic boom in the period from the late 40s through the 70s

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that created a kind of mass middle class in many societies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So capitalism rose from the ashes, as it were.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And this changed the game for Stalin and communism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Communism is about an alternative to capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And if that alternative is not superior, there's no reason for communism to exist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But if capitalism is in foul odor, if people have a bad opinion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: a strong critique of capitalism, there can be appeal to alternatives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And that's kind of what happened with Stalin's rule.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But after World War II, the context changed a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Capitalism was very different, much more successful, nonviolent compared to what it was in the interwar period.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And the Soviet Union had a tough time competing against that new context.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Now today we see similarly that the image and reality of capitalism is on the question again,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: which leads some people to find an answer in socialism as an alternative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So you just kind of painted a beautiful picture of comparison.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: This is the way we think about ideologies, because we is what's working better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Do you separate in your mind the ideals of communism to the Stalinist implementation of communism?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And again, capitalism and American implementation of capitalism?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And as we look at now the 21st century, where yes, this idea of socialism being a potential political system

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: or economic system would operate in the United States rising up again as an idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So how do we think about that again in the 21st century, about these ideas, fundamental deep ideas of communism and capitalism?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Yeah. So in the Marxist schema, there was something called feudalism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: which was supposedly destroyed by the bourgeoisie who created capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And then the working class was supposed to destroy capitalism and create socialism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But socialism wasn't the end stage. The end stage was going to be communism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So that's why the Communist Party in the Soviet Union first built socialism, transcending capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The next stage was socialism and the end game, the final stage was communism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So their version of socialism was derived from Marx.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And Marx argued that the problem was capitalism had been very beneficial for a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It had produced greater wealth and greater opportunity than feudalism had.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But then it had come to serve only the narrow interests of the so-called bourgeoisie or the capitalists themselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so for humanity's sake, the universal class, the working class needed to overthrow capitalism

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: in order for greater productivity, greater wealth to be produced for all of humanity to flourish and on a higher level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So you couldn't have socialism unless you destroyed capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So that meant no markets, no private property, no so-called parliaments or bourgeois parliaments, as they were called.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So you got socialism in Marx's schema by transcending, by eliminating capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Now, Marx also called for freedom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He said that this elimination of markets and private property and bourgeois parliaments would produce greater freedom in addition to greater abundance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: However, everywhere this was tried, it produced tyranny and mass violence, death and shortages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Everywhere it was tried. There's no exception in historical terms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so it's very interesting. Marx insisted that capitalism had to be eliminated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You couldn't have markets. Markets were chaos. You needed planning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You couldn't have hiring of wage labor. That was wage slavery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You couldn't have private property because that was a form of theft.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So in the Marxist scheme, somehow you were going to eliminate capitalism and get to freedom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It turned out you didn't get to freedom. So then people said, well, you can't blame Marx because he said we needed freedom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He was pro-freedom. So it's kind of like dropping a nuclear bomb.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You say you're going to drop a nuclear bomb, but you want to minimize civilian casualties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So the dropping of the nuclear bomb is the elimination of markets, private property and parliaments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But you're going to bring freedom or you're going to minimize civilian casualties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So you drop the nuclear bomb, you eliminate the capitalism, and you get famine, deportation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: no constraints on executive power and not abundance, but shortages.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And people say, well, that's not what I, Mark said. That's not what I said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I said I wanted to minimize civilian casualties. The nuclear bomb goes off and there's mass civilian casualties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And you keep saying, but I said drop the bomb, but minimize civilian casualties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So that's where we are. That's history, not philosophy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I'm speaking about historical examples, all the cases that we have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Marx was not a theorist of inequality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Marx was a theorist of alienation, of dehumanization, of fundamental constraints

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: or what he called fetters on productivity and on wealth, which he all attributed to capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Marx wasn't bothered by inequality. He was bothered by something deeper, something worse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Those socialists who figured this out, who understood that if you drop the nuclear bomb,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: there was no way to minimize civilian casualties.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Those socialists who came to understand that if you eliminated capitalism, markets, private property, and parliaments,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: if you eliminated that, you wouldn't get freedom.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Those Marxists, those socialists became what we would call social democrats

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: or people who would use the state to regulate the market, not to eliminate the market.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: They would use the state to redistribute income, not to destroy private property and markets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so this in the Marxist schema was apostasy because they were accepting markets and private property.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: They were accepting alienation and wage slavery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: They were accepting capitalism in principle, but they wanted to fix it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: They wanted to ameliorate. They wanted to regulate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so they became what was denounced as revisionists, not true Marxists, not real revolutionaries,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but parliamentary road, parliamentarians.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: We know this as normal politics, normal social democratic politics from the European case or from the American case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But they are not asking to eliminate capitalism, blaming capitalism, blaming markets and private property.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So this rift among the socialists, the ones who were for elimination of capitalism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: transcending capitalism, otherwise you could never ever get to abundance and freedom in the Marxist schema,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: versus those who accept capitalism but want to regulate and redistribute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: That rift on the left has been with us almost from the beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It's a kind of civil war on the left between the Leninists and the social democrats

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: or the revisionists as they're known pejoratively by the Leninists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: We have the same confusion today in the world today,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: where people also cite Marx saying capitalism is a dead end

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and we need to drop that nuclear bomb and get freedom, get no civilian casualties,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: versus those who say, yes, there are inequities, there's a lack of equality of opportunity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: there are many other issues that we need to deal with and we can fix those issues, we can regulate, we can redistribute.
