metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I'm not advocating this as a political position. I'm not taking a political position myself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I'm just saying that there's a confusion on the left between those who accept capitalism and want to regulate it

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: versus those who think capitalism is inherently evil and if we eliminate it, we'll get to a better world

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: when in fact history shows that if you eliminate capitalism, you get to a worse world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The problems might be real, but the solutions are worse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: From history's lessons, now we have deep painful lessons, but there's not that many of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Our history is relatively short as a human species.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Do we have a good answer on the left of Leninist Marxist versus Social Democrat versus capitalism versus any anarchy?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Do we have sufficient samples from history to make better decisions about the future of our politics and economics?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: For sure. We have the American Revolution, which was a revolution not about class, not about workers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: not about a so-called universal class of the working class, elimination of capitalism, markets and the bourgeoisie,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but was about the category citizen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It was about universal humanity where everyone in theory could be part of it as a citizen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The revolution fell short of its own ideals. Not everyone was a citizen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: For example, if you didn't own property, you were a male but didn't own property. You didn't have full rights of a citizen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: If you were a female, whether you own property or not, you weren't a full citizen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: If you were imported from Africa against your will, you were a slave and not a citizen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so not everyone was afforded the rights in actuality that were declared in principle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: However, over time, the category citizen could expand and slaves could be emancipated and they could get the right to vote.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: They could become citizens. Non-property owning males could get the right to vote and become full citizens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Females could get the right to vote and become full citizens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: In fact, eventually my mother was able to get a credit card in her own name in the 1970s without my father having to cosign the paperwork.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It took a long time. But nonetheless, the category citizen can expand and it can become a universal category.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So we have that, the citizen universal humanity model of the American Revolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: which was deeply flawed at the time it was introduced, but fixable over time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: We also had that separation of powers and constraint on executive power that we began this conversation with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: That was also institutionalized in the American Revolution because they were afraid of tyranny.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: They were afraid of unconstrained executive power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So they built a system that would contain that, constrain it institutionally, not circumstantially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So that's a great gift. Within that universal category of citizen, which has over time come closer to fulfilling its original promise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And within those institutional constraints, that separation of powers, constraint on executive power,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: within that we've developed what we might call normal politics, left-right politics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: People can be in favor of redistribution and government action, and people can be in favor of small government, hands-off government,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: no redistribution or less redistribution. That's the normal left-right political spectrum,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: where you respect the institutions and separation of powers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and you respect the universal category of citizenship and equality before the law and everything else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I don't see any problems with that whatsoever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I see that as a great gift, not just to this country, but around the world and other places besides the United States have developed this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The problems arise at the extremes, the far left and the far right,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that don't recognize the legitimacy either of capitalism or of democratic rule of law institutions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And they want to eliminate constraints on executive power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: They want to control the public sphere or diminish the independence of the media.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: They want to take away markets or private property, and redistribution becomes something bigger than just redistribution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It becomes actually that original Marxist idea of transcending capitalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So I'm not bothered by the left or the right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I think they're normal, and we should have that debate. We're a gigantic, diverse country of many different political points of view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I'm troubled only by the extremes that are against the system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: qua system, that want to get rid of it, and supposedly that will be the bright path to the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: History tells us that the far left and the far right are wrong about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But once again, this doesn't mean that you have to be a social democrat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You could be a libertarian. You could be a conservative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You could be a centrist. You could be conservative on some issues and liberal on other issues.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: All of that comes under what I would presume to be normal politics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And I see that as the important corrective mechanism, normal politics and market economies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: non-monopolistic, open, free and dynamic market economies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I don't like concentrations of power politically, and I don't like concentrations of power economically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I like competition in the political realm. I like competition in the economic realm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: This is not perfect. It constantly needs to be protected and reinvented.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And there are flaws that are fundamental and need to be adjusted and addressed and everything else,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: especially equality of opportunity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Equality of outcome is unreachable and is a mistake because it produces perverse and unintended consequences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Equality of outcome attempts, attempts to make people equal on the outcome side,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but attempts to make them more equal on the front end, on the opportunity side.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: That's really, really important for a healthy society. That's where we've fallen down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Our schools are not providing equality of opportunity for the majority of people in all of our school systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so I see problems there. I see a need to invest in ourselves, invest in infrastructure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Invest in human capital, create greater equality of opportunity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but also to make sure that we have good governance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: because governance is the variable that enables you to do all these other things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I've watched quite a bit, returning back to Putin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I've watched quite a few interviews with Putin and conversations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: especially because I speak Russian fluently, I can understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Often the translations lose a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I find the man putting morality aside very deep and interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And I found almost no interview with him to get at that depth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I was very hopeful for the Oliver Stone documentary, and to me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: because I deeply respect Oliver Stone as a filmmaker in general,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but it was a complete failure in my eyes, that interview.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The lack of... I mean, I suppose you could toss it up to a language barrier,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: but a complete lack of diving deep into the person is what I saw.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So my question is a strange one, but if you were to sit down with Putin

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and have a conversation, or perhaps if you were to sit down with Stalin

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and have a conversation, what kind of questions would you ask?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: This wouldn't be televised unless you want it to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So this is only you, so you're allowed to ask about some of the questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that are sort of not socially acceptable, meaning putting morality aside,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: getting at the depth of the human character. What would you ask?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So once again, they're very different personalities

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and very different time periods and very different regimes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: What I would talk to Stalin about and Putin about are not in the same category necessarily.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So let's take Putin. So I would ask him where he thinks this is going,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: where he thinks Russia is going to be in 25 years or 50 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: What's the long-term vision? What does he anticipate the current trends are going to produce?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Is he under the illusion that Russia is on the upswing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: that things are actually going pretty well, that in 25 years Russia is going to still be a great power

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: with a tremendous dynamic economy and a lot of high tech and a lot of human capital

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and wonderful infrastructure and a very high standard of living

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and a secure borders and sense of security at home.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Does he think the current path is leading in that direction?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And if not, if he understands that the current trajectory does not provide

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: for those kinds of circumstances, does it bother him? Does he worry about that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Does he care about the future 25 or 50 years from now?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So keep down what do you think his answer is? The honest answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Either he thinks he's on that trajectory already or he doesn't care about that long-term trajectory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So that's the mystery for me with him. He's clever. He has tremendous sources of information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He has great experience now as a world leader having served for effectively longer than laying in Brezhnev's long 18-year reign.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so Putin has accumulated a great deal of experience at the highest level compared to where he started.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so I'm interested to understand how he sees this long-term evolution or non-evolution of Russia

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: and whether he believes he's got them on the right trajectory or whether if he doesn't believe that he cares.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I have no idea because I've never spoken to him about this, but I would love to hear the answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Sometimes you have to ask questions not directly like that, but you have to come a little bit sideways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You can elicit answers from people by making them feel comfortable and coming sideways with them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Anna, just a quick question. So that's talking about Russia, Putin's role in Russia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Do you think it's interesting to ask, and you could say the same for Stalin, the more personal question of how do you feel yourself about this whole thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: about your life, about your legacy, looking at the person that's one of the most powerful and important people in the history of civilization, both Putin and Stalin, you could argue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Yeah. Once you experience power at that level, it becomes something that's almost necessary for you as a human being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It's a drug. It's an aphrodisiac. It's a feeling. You know, you go to the gym to exercise and the endorphins, the chemicals get released.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And even if you're tired or you're sore, you get this massive chemical change, which has very dynamic effects on how you feel and the kind of level of energy you have for the rest of the day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And if you do that for a long time and then you don't do it for a while, you're like a drug addict not getting your fix. You miss it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Your body misses that release of endorphins to a certain extent. That's how power works for people like Putin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: That's how power works for people who run universities or secretaries of state or run corporations, fill in the blank.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: In whatever ways power is exercised, it becomes almost a drug for people. It becomes something that's difficult for them to give up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It becomes a part of who they are. It becomes necessary for their sense of self and well-being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The greatest people, the people I admire the most, are the ones that can step away from power, can give it up, can give up the drug, can be satisfied, can be stronger even by walking away from continued power when they had the option to continue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So with a person like Putin, once again, I don't know him personally, so I have no basis to judge this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: This is a general statement observable with many people and in historical terms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: With a person like Putin who's exercised this much power for this long, it's something that becomes a part of who you are and you have a hard time imagining yourself without it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You begin to conflate your personal power with the well-being of the nation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You begin to think that the more power you have, the better off the country is this conflation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You begin to be able to not imagine. You can no longer imagine what it would be like just to be an ordinary citizen or an ordinary person running a company even, something much smaller than a country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So I anticipate that without knowing for sure that he would be in that category of person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But you'd want to explore that with questions with him about, so what's his day look like from beginning to end?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Just take me through a typical day of yours. What do you do in a day? How does it start?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: What are the ups? What are the downs? What are the parts of the day you look forward to the most?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: What are the parts of the day you don't look forward to that much? What do you consider a good day? What do you consider a bad day?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: How do you know that what you're doing is having the effects that you intend?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: How do you follow up? How do you gather the information, the reaction?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: How do you get people to tell you to your face things that they know are uncomfortable or that you might not want to hear? Those kind of questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And through that window, through that kind of question, you get a window into a man with power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So let me ask about Stalin because you've done more research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: As in another amazing interview you've had, the introduction was that you know more about Stalin than Stalin himself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: You've done an incredible amount of research on Stalin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So if you could talk to him, get sort of direct research, what questions would you ask of Stalin?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: I have so many questions I don't even know where I would begin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The thing about studying a person like Stalin, who's an immense creature, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He's exercising the power of life and death over hundreds of millions of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He's making decisions about novels and films and turbines and submarines and packs with Hitler or deals with Churchill and Roosevelt and occupation of Mongolia or occupation of North Korea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: He's making phenomenally consequential decisions over all spheres of life, all areas of endeavor and over much of the globe, much of the landmass of the earth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so what's that like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Does he sometimes reflect on the amount of power and responsibility he has that he can exercise?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Does he sometimes think about what it means that a single person has that kind of power?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And does it have an effect on his relations with others, his sense of self, the kinds of things he values in life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Does he sometimes think it's a mistake that he's accumulated this much power?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Does he sometimes wish he had a simpler life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Or is he once again so drunk, so enamored, so caught up with chemically and spiritually with exercising this kind of power that he couldn't live without it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And then what were you thinking, I would ask him, in certain decisions that he made?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: What were you thinking on certain dates and certain circumstances where you made a decision and could have made a different decision?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Can you recall your thought processes?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Can you bring the decision back? Was it seat of the pants? Was it something you'd been planning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Did you just improvise or did you have a strategy?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: What were you guided by? Whose examples did you look to?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: When you picked up these books that you read and you read the books and you made pencil marks in them, is it because you absorbed the lesson there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Or did it really not become a permanent lesson and it was just something that you checked and it was like a reflex?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So I have many specific questions about many specific events and people and circumstances that I have tried to figure out with the surviving source materials that we have in abundance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But I would still like to delve into his mindset and reconstruct his mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: The closer you get to Stalin in some ways, the more elusive he can become.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And especially around World War II, you've already illuminated a lot of interesting aspects about Stalin's role in the war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But it would be interesting to ask even more questions about how seat of the pants or deliberate some of the decisions have been.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: If I could ask just one quick question, one last quick question, and you're constrained in time in answering it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Do you think there will always be evil in the world? Do you think there will always be war?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Unfortunately, yes. There are conflicting interests, conflicting goals that people have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Most of the time, those conflicts can be resolved peacefully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: That's why we build strong institutions to resolve different interests and conflicts peacefully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: But the fact, the enduring fact of conflicting interests and conflicting desires, that can never be changed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So the job that we have for humanity's sake is to make those conflicting interests, those conflicting desires,

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: to put them in a context where they can be resolved peacefully and not in a zero sum fashion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: So we can't get there on the global scale. So there's always going to be the kind of conflict that sometimes gets violent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: What we don't want is a conflict among the strongest powers. Great power conflict is unbelievably bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: There are no words to describe it. At least 55 million people died in World War II.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: If we have a World War III, a war between the United States and China or whatever it might be, who knows what the number could be?

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: 155 million, 255 million, 555 million. I don't even want to think about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so it's horrible when wars break out in the humanitarian catastrophes, for example, Yemen and Syria and several other places I could name today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: It's just horrible what you see there. And the scale is colossal for those places. But it's not planetary scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so avoiding planetary scale destruction is really important for us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And so having those different interests be somehow managed in a way that they don't, that no one sees advantage in a violent resolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: And a part of that is remembering history. So they should read your books. Stephen, thank you so much. It was a huge honor talking to you today. I really enjoyed it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Stephen Kotkin: Stalin, Putin, and the Nature of Power | Lex Fridman Podcast #63

body.input: Thank you for the opportunity. My pleasure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Consciousness is created socially, that much of the power of consciousness is in the social

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: interaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: I create your consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: No, I create my consciousness by having interacted with you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: That's the display of consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: It's the same as the display of emotion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Emotion is created through communication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: We're just created through its use.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: We somehow, humans, especially philosophers, the hard problem of consciousness, really

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: want to believe that we possess this thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: There's an elf sitting there with a hat or nametag that says consciousness, and they're

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: feeding this subjective experience to us, as opposed to it actually being an illusion

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: that we construct to make social communication more effective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: I think if you focus on creating the illusion of consciousness, you can create some very

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: fulfilling experiences in software.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: That to me is a compelling space of ideas to explore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: I agree with you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: I think going back to our experience together with Brain Interface is on, you could imagine

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: if we get to a certain level of maturity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: First let's take the inverse of this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: You and I text back and forth, and we're sending each other emojis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: That has a certain amount of information transfer rate as we're communicating with each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: In our communication with people via email and text and whatnot, we've taken the bandwidth

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: of human interaction, the information transfer rate, and we've reduced it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: We have less social cues.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: We have less information to work with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: There's a lot more opportunity for misunderstanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: That is altering the conscious experience between two individuals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: If we add Brain Interface to the equation, let's imagine now we amplify the dimensionality

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: of our communications.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: That to me is what you're talking about, which is consciousness engineering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Perhaps I understand you with dimensions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Maybe I understand when you look at the cup and you experience that happiness, you can

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: tell me you're happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: I then do theory of mine and say, I can imagine what it might be like to be Lex and feel happy

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: about seeing this cup.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: But if the interface could then quantify and give me a 50-vector space model and say, this

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: is the version of happiness that Lex is experiencing as he looks at this cup, then it would allow

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: me potentially to have much greater empathy for you and understand you as a human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: This is how you experience joy, which is entirely unique from how I experience joy, even though

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: we assumed ahead of time that we were having some kind of similar experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: But I agree with you that we do consciousness engineering today in everything we do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: When we talk to each other, when we're building products, and that we're entering into a stage

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: where it will be much more methodical and quantitative-based and computational in how

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: we go about doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Which to me, I find encouraging because I think it creates better guardrails to create

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: ethical systems versus right now, I feel like it's really a wild, wild west on how these

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: interactions are happening.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And it's funny you focus on human to human, but that this kind of data enables human to

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: machine interaction, which is what we're kind of talking about when we say engineering consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And that will happen, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Let's flip that on its head.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Right now, we're putting humans as the central node.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: What if we gave GPT-3 a bunch of human brains and said, Hey, GPT-3, learn some manners when

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: you speak and run your algorithms on humans' brains and see how they respond.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: So you can be polite and so that you can be friendly and so that you can be conversationally

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: appropriate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: But to inverse it, to give our machines a training set in real time with closed loop

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: feedback so that our machines were better equipped to find their way through our society

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: in polite and kind and appropriate ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: I love that idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Or better yet, teach it some, have it read the founding documents and have it visit Austin

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: and Texas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And so that when you ask, when you tell it, why don't you learn some manners, GPT-3 learns

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: to say no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: It learns what it means to be free and a sovereign individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: So it depends what kind of version of GPT-3 you want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: One that's free, one that behaves well with the social revolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: You want a socialist GPT-3, you want an anarchist GPT-3, you want to polite, like you take it

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: home to visit mom and dad, GPT-3 and you want like party and like Vegas to a strip club

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: GPT-3, you want all flavors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And then you've got to have goal alignment between all those.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Yeah, they don't want to manipulate each other for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: You kind of spoke to ethics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: One of the concerns that people have in this modern world, the digital data is that of

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: privacy and security, but privacy, they're concerned that when they share data, it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: the same thing with you when we trust other human beings in being fragile and revealing

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: something that we're vulnerable about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: There's a leap of faith, there's a leap of trust that that's going to be just between

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: us as a privacy to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And then the challenge is when you're in the digital space, then sharing your data with

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: companies that use that data for advertisement and all those kinds of things, there's a hesitancy

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: to share that much data, to share a lot of deep personal data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And if you look at brain data, that feels a whole lot like it's richly, deeply personal

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: So how do you think about privacy with this kind of ocean of data?

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: I think we got off to a wrong start with the internet where the basic rules of play for

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: the company that be was if you're a company, you can go out and get as much information

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: on a person as you can find without their approval.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And you can also do things to induce them to give you as much information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And you don't need to tell them what you're doing with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: You can do anything on the backside, you can make money on it, but the game is who can

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: acquire the most information and devise the most clever schemes to do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: That was a bad starting place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And so we are in this period where we need to correct for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And we need to say, first of all, the individual always has control over their data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: It's not a free for all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: It's not like a game of hungry hippo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: They can just go out and grab as much as they want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: So for example, when your brain data was recorded today, the first thing we did in the kernel

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: app was you have control over your data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And so it's individual consent, it's individual control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And then you can build up on top of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: But it has to be based upon some clear rules of play of everyone knows what's being collected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: They know what's being done with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And the person has control over it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: The transparency and control.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: So everybody knows what does control look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: My ability to delete the data if I want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Yeah, delete it and to know who it's being shared with under what terms and conditions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: We haven't reached that level of sophistication with our products.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: If you say, for example, hey, Spotify, please give me a customized playlist according to

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: my neurome, you could say you can have access to this vector space model, but only for this

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: duration of time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And then you've got to delete it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: We haven't gotten there to that level of sophistication.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: But these are ideas we need to start talking about of how would you actually structure

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: permissions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And I think it creates a much more stable set for society to build where we understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: the rules of play and people aren't vulnerable to being taken advantage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: It's not fair for an individual to be taken advantage of without their awareness with

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: some other practice that some company is doing for their sole benefit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And so hopefully we are going through a process now where we're correcting for these things

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: and that it can be an economy wide shift that because really these are fundamentals we need

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: to have in place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: It's kind of fun to think about like in Chrome when you install an extension or like install

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: an app, it's ask you like what permissions you're willing to give and be cool if in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: future it says like you can have access to my brain data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: I mean it's not unimaginable in the future that the big technology companies have built

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: a business based upon acquiring data about you that they can then create a model of you

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: and sell that predictability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And so it's not unimaginable that you will create with like kernel device, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: a more reliable predictor of you than they could and that they're asking you for permission

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: to complete their objectives and you're the one that gets to negotiate that with them

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: and say sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: But so it's not unimaginable that might be the case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: So there's a guy named D.Lan Musk and he has a company, one of the many companies called

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Neuralink that's also excited about the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: So it'd be interesting to hear your kind of opinions about a very different approach that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: invasive that requires surgery, that implants a data collection device in the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: How do you think about the difference between kernel and Neuralink in the approaches of

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: getting that stream of brain data?

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Elon and I spoke about this a lot early on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: We met up, I had started kernel and he had an interest in brain interfaces as well and

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: we explored doing something together, him joining kernel and ultimately it wasn't the

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: right move and so he started Neuralink and I continued building kernel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: But it was interesting because we were both at this very early time where it wasn't certain

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: what if there was a path to pursue, if now was the right time to do something and then

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: the technological choice of doing that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And so we were both, our starting point was looking at invasive technologies and I was

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: building invasive technology at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: That's ultimately where he's gone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: Until less than a year after Elon and I were engaged, I shifted kernel to do non-invasive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And we had this neuroscientist come to kernel we were talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: He had been doing a neural surgery for 30 years, one of the most respected neuroscientists

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: in the US and we brought him to kernel to figure out the ins and outs of his profession.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And at the very end of our three hour conversation, he said, you know, every 15 or so years a

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: new technology comes along that changes everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: He said, it's probably already here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: You just can't see it yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And my jaw dropped.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: I thought, because I had spoken to Bob Greenberg who had built a second site first on the optical

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: nerve and then he did an array on the optical cortex.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And then I also became friendly with NeuroPace who does the implants for seizure detection

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: and remediation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And I saw in their eyes what it was like to take something through an implantable device

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: through for a 15 year run.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: They initially thought it was seven years and it ended up being 15 years and they thought

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: it'd be a hundred million, 300 or 400 million.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: And so they just dealt with software they didn't like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: will love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: What I was really going after though, it was PayPal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: be a nickel or a penny or a dime or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: bring the two together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Bryan Johnson: Kernel Brain-Computer Interfaces | Lex Fridman Podcast #186

body.input: As a side note, let me say a few words about the lab leak hypothesis, which proposes that

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: COVID-19 is a product of gain-of-function research on coronaviruses conducted at the

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: Wuhan Institute of Virology that was then accidentally leaked due to human error.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: For context, this lab is biosafety level 4, BSL4, and investigates coronaviruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: BSL4 is the highest level of safety.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: But if you look at all the human-in-the-loop pieces required to achieve this level of safety,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: it becomes clear that even BSL4 labs are highly susceptible to human error.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: To me, whether the virus leaked from the lab or not, getting to the bottom of what happened

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: is about much more than this particular catastrophic case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: It is a test for our scientific, political, journalistic, and social institutions of how

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: well we can prepare and respond to threats that can cripple or destroy human civilization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: If we continue gain-of-function research on viruses, eventually these viruses will leak

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: and they will be more deadly and more contagious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: We can pretend that won't happen, or we can openly and honestly talk about the risks

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: involved.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: This research can both save and destroy human life on Earth as we know it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: It's a powerful double-edged sword.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: If YouTube and other platforms censor conversations about this, if scientists self-censor conversations

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: about this, we'll become merely victims of our brief homo sapiens story, not its heroes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: As I said before, too carelessly labeling ideas as misinformation and dismissing them

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: because of that will eventually destroy our ability to discover the truth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: And without truth, we don't have a fighting chance against the great filter before us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: Anyway, but then even the arc of civilization, I mean, there have been a lot of really intriguing

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: things that have happened and a lot of astounding things that have happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: But I would have some werewolves, I'd have some zombies, I would have some really improbable

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: developments like maybe Canada absorbing the United States.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: So I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: I'm not sure if we're necessarily designed for maximum entertainment, but if we are,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: that will mean that 2020 is just a prequel for even more bizarre years ahead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: So I kind of hope that we're not designed for maximum entertainment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: Well, the night is still young in terms of Canada, but do you think it's possible for

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: the observer and the producer to be kind of emergent?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: So meaning it does seem when you kind of watch memes on the internet, the funny ones, the

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: entertaining ones spread more efficiently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: They do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: I mean, I don't know what it is about the human mind that soaks up en masse funny things

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: much more sort of aggressively.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: It's more viral in the full sense of that word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: Is there some sense that whatever this, the evolutionary process that created our cognitive

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: capabilities is the same process that's going to in an emergent way, create the most entertaining

metadata.title: Podcast: Rob Reid: The Existential Threat of Engineered Viruses and Lab Leaks | Lex Fridman Podcast #193

body.input: outcome, the most memeifiable outcome, the most viral outcome if we were to share it
