metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: And that's kind of maybe a long-winded way of saying it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: but to learn, I think I'll try to say it simply,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: there's a five step process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: Step one is know your goals, know what you're going after.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: You could have almost anything you want,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: but you can't have everything you want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: And so you have to prioritize and you move in that direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: On the way to your goals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: you're going to encounter your problems and your obstacles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: So identifying, step two is understanding your problems

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: and your obstacles, identify them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: Step three is to diagnose them to get at the root cause

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: of the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: And that could be many root causes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: but it could also be your weaknesses or weaknesses of others,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: but you have to be objective about them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: Once you diagnose them, then you go to step four,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: which is to design a way to get around them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: And then after you have that design,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: you implement that design.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: So you have to follow through and do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: And you do that and that will then produce its new results,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: which should be better results.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: I call this kind of a looping process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: It's the evolutionary looping process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: And you just keep doing that and you learn

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: over a period of time and you move

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: in the direction that you want.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: who will be participants in the continuation of the story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: May the force of evolution be with you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: taking human civilization and what in this story

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: that evolution is writing gives you hope?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: Evolution is in a direction toward improvement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: And the greatest force is a man's capacity

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: to adapt and invent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: And so you see in the charts in the book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: you see that this upward movement,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: life expectancy, health,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: all the things that we think are better,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: you see there's a chart and it shows

body.input: that over a period of time and you barely see

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: the downturns from depressions and wars in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: That is the greatest power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: Man's ability to invent and adapt is evolution

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: and that's the greatest power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: And that is what gives me justifiable hope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: And a continuation of that, like we mentioned with Elon,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: maybe we'll become a multi-planetary species.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ray Dalio: Money, Power, and the Collapse of Empires | Lex Fridman Podcast #251

body.input: So you have supervised.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: And then unsupervised basically means everything

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: which is not supervised,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: but that includes stuff like semi-supervised

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: it has a sort of higher probability density

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: I mean, the easier example,

body.input: which is not as widely used these days is basically say,

body.input: for example, video prediction.

body.input: So video is again, a sequence of things.

body.input: And the idea basically is because the model is predicting

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Because the model is predicting what's happening there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: is something called the self-attention model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: And the idea basically is that if you have N elements,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So a lot of these people have been

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: sort of showing results in this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Of course, I was aware of this result,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: but I wasn't really sure how well it would work in practice

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: for like other sort of downstream tasks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So the results kept getting better

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: and I wasn't sure if like a lot of our insights

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: from self-supervised learning would translate

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: into this multimodal learning problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So multimodal learning is when you have like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: when you have multiple modalities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: That's not even possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Okay, so the particular modalities that we worked on

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: in this work were audio and video.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So the idea was basically if you have a video,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: you have its corresponding audio track

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: and you want to use both of these signals,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: the audio signal and the video signal

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: to learn a good representation for video

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: and good representation for audio.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Like this podcast. Like this podcast, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So what we did in this work was basically trained

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: two different neural networks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: one on the video signal, one on the audio signal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: And what we wanted is basically the features

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: that we get from both of these neural networks

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: should be similar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So it should basically be able to produce

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: the same kinds of features from the video

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: and the same kinds of features from the audio.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Now, why is this useful?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Well, for a lot of these objects that we have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: there is a characteristic sound, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So trains, when they go by,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: they make a particular kind of sound.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Boats make a particular kind of sound.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: People, when they're jumping around,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: will like shout, whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Bananas don't make a sound.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So where you can't learn anything about bananas there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Or when humans mention bananas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Well, yes, when they say the word banana, then-

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So you can't trust basically anything

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: that comes out of a human's mouth

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: as that source of audio is useless.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So the typical use case is basically like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: for example, someone playing a musical instrument.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So guitars have a particular kind of sound and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So because a lot of these things are correlated,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: the idea in multimodal learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: is to take these two kinds of modalities,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: video and audio, and learn a common embedding space,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: a common feature space where both of these related modalities

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: can basically be close together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: And again, you use contrastive learning for this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So in contrastive learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: basically the video and the corresponding audio

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: are positives, and you can take any other video

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: or any other audio, and that becomes a negative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: And so basically that's it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: It's just a simple application of contrastive learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: The main sort of finding from this work for us

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: was basically that you can actually learn

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: very, very powerful feature representations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: very, very powerful video representations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: So you can learn the sort of video network

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: that we ended up learning can actually be used

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: for downstream, for example, recognizing human actions

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: or recognizing different types of sounds, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Right, so there is this data set called Kinetics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: that you learn in a self-supervised way

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: I told you I'm doing this podcast to try to get the answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: I'm hoping you could tell me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: What do you think the meaning of it all is?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: I don't think I figured this out, no, I have no idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Do you think AI will help us figure it out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Or do you think there's no answer?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: The whole point is to keep searching.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: I think, yeah, I think it's an endless sort of quest for us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: I don't think AI will help us there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: This is like a very hard, hard, hard question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: which so many humans have tried to answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Well, that's the interesting thing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: difference between AI and humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Humans don't seem to know what the hell they're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: And AI is almost always operating

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: under well-defined objective functions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: to define good long-term objective functions

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: under which we operate, if that's a feature or a bug?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: I would say it's a feature

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: because then everyone actually has very different kinds

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: of objective functions that they're optimizing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: And those objective functions evolve

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: and like change dramatically

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: through their course of their life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: That's actually what makes us interesting, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: If otherwise, like if everyone was doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: the exact same thing, that would be pretty boring.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: We do want like people

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: with different kinds of perspectives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: Also people evolve continuously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: That's like, I would say the biggest feature of being human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: And as a species, we take that lesson

metadata.title: Podcast: Ishan Misra: Self-Supervised Deep Learning in Computer Vision | Lex Fridman Podcast #206

body.input: and become better and better

body.input: You've studied the human mind, cognition, language, vision, evolution, psychology from child to adult,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: from the level of individual to the level of our entire civilization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: So I feel like I can start with a simple multiple choice question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: What is the meaning of life? Is it A. to attain knowledge as Plato said, B. to attain power as

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Nietzsche said, C. to escape death as Ernest Becker said, D. to propagate our genes as

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Darwin and others have said, E. there is no meaning as the nihilists have said, F. knowing the meaning

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: of life is beyond our cognitive capabilities as Stephen Pinker said based on my interpretation

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: 20 years ago, and G. none of the above. I'd say A comes closest but I would amend that to

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: attaining not only knowledge but fulfillment more generally. That is life, health, stimulation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: access to the living cultural and social world. Now this is our meaning of life. It's not the

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: meaning of life if you were to ask our genes. Their meaning is to propagate copies of themselves

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: but that is distinct from the meaning that the brain that they lead to sets for itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: So to you knowledge is a small subset or a large subset?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: It's a large subset but it's not the entirety of human striving because we also want to

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: interact with people. We want to experience beauty. We want to experience the richness

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: of the natural world but understanding what makes the universe tick is way up there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: For some of us more than others, certainly for me that's one of the top five.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: So is that a fundamental aspect? Are you just describing your own preference or is this a

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: fundamental aspect of human nature is to seek knowledge? In your latest book you talk about

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: the power, the usefulness of rationality and reason and so on. Is that a fundamental nature

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: of human beings or is it something we should just strive for?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Both. We're capable of striving for it because it is one of the things that

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: make us what we are, homo sapiens, wise men. We are unusual among animals in the degree to

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: which we acquire knowledge and use it to survive. We make tools. We strike agreements via language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: We extract poisons. We predict the behavior of animals. We try to get at the workings of plants

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: and when I say we, I don't just mean we in the modern West but we as a species everywhere,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: which is how we've managed to occupy every niche on the planet, how we've managed to drive other

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: animals to extinction and the refinement of reason in pursuit of human well-being, of

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: health, happiness, social richness, cultural richness is our main challenge in the present.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: That is using our intellect, using our knowledge to figure out how the world works, how we work

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: in order to make discoveries and strike agreements that make us all better off in the long run.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Right. You do that almost undeniably and in a data-driven way in your recent book,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: but I'd like to focus on the artificial intelligence aspect of things and not just

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: artificial intelligence but natural intelligence too. So 20 years ago in the book you've written

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: on how the mind works. You conjecture, again, am I right to interpret things? You can correct me

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: if I'm wrong, but you conjecture that human thought in the brain may be a result of a massive

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: network of highly interconnected neurons. So from this interconnectivity emerges thought.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Compared to artificial neural networks we use for machine learning today, is there something

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: fundamentally more complex, mysterious, even magical about the biological neural networks

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: versus the ones we've been starting to use over the past 60 years and have become to success in

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: the past 10? There is something a little bit mysterious about the human neural networks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: which is that each one of us who is a neural network knows that we ourselves are conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Conscious not in the sense of registering our surroundings or even registering our internal

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: state, but in having subjective first-person present tense experience. That is, when I see red,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: it's not just different from green, but there's a redness to it that I feel. Whether an artificial

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: system would experience that or not, I don't know and I don't think I can know. That's why it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: mysterious. If we had a perfectly lifelike robot that was behaviorally indistinguishable from a

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: human, would we attribute consciousness to it or ought we to attribute consciousness to it? That's

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: something that it's very hard to know. But putting that aside, putting aside that largely

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: philosophical question, the question is, is there some difference between the human neural network

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: and the ones that we're building in artificial intelligence will mean that we're on the current

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: trajectory not going to reach the point where we've got a lifelike robot indistinguishable

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: from a human because the way their so-called neural networks are organized are different from

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: the way ours are organized. I think there's overlap, but I think there are some big differences

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: that the current neural networks, current so-called deep learning systems are in reality not all that

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: deep. That is, they are very good at extracting high order statistical regularities, but most of

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: the systems don't have a semantic level, a level of actual understanding of who did what to whom,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: why, where, how things work, what causes what else. Do you think that kind of thing can emerge

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: as it does? So artificial neural networks are much smaller, the number of connections and so on than

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: the current human biological networks, but do you think sort of to go to consciousness or to go to

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: this higher level semantic reasoning about things, do you think that can emerge with just a larger

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: network, with a more richly, weirdly interconnected network? Separate it in consciousness because

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: consciousness is even a matter of complexity. A really weird one. Yeah, you could have, you could

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: sensibly ask the question of whether shrimp are conscious, for example. They're not terribly

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: complex, but maybe they feel pain. So let's just put that part of it aside. But I think sheer size

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: of a neural network is not enough to give it structure and knowledge, but if it's suitably

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: engineered, then why not? That is, we're neural networks, natural selection did a kind of equivalent

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: of engineering of our brains. So I don't think there's anything mysterious in the sense that no

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: system made out of silicon could ever do what a human brain can do. I think it's possible in

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: principle. Whether it'll ever happen depends not only on how clever we are in engineering these

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: systems, but whether even we even want to, whether that's even a sensible goal. That is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: you can ask the question, is there any locomotion system that is as good as a human? Well, we kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: of want to do better than a human, ultimately, in terms of legged locomotion. There's no reason

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: that humans should be our benchmark. They're tools that might be better in some ways. It may be just

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: be not as, it may be that we can't duplicate a natural system because at some point it's so much

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: cheaper to use a natural system that we're not going to invest more brain power and resources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: So for example, we don't really have an exact substitute for wood. We still build houses out

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: of wood. We still build furniture out of wood. We like the look. We like the feel. It would have

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: certain properties that synthetics don't. It's not that there's anything magical or mysterious about

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: wood. It's just that the extra steps of duplicating everything about wood is something we just haven't

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: bothered because we have wood. Likewise, say cotton. I mean, I'm wearing cotton clothing now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: It feels much better than polyester. It's not that cotton has something magic in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: It's not that we couldn't ever synthesize something exactly like cotton, but at some point,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: it's just not worth it. We've got cotton. Likewise, in the case of human intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: the goal of making an artificial system that is exactly like the human brain is a goal that we

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: probably no one is going to pursue to the bitter end, I suspect. Because if you want tools that do

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: things better than humans, you're not going to care whether it does something like humans. So for

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: example, diagnosing cancer or predicting the weather, why set humans as your benchmark?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: But in general, I suspect you also believe that even if the human should not be a benchmark,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: we don't want to imitate humans in their system. There's a lot to be learned about how to create

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: an artificial intelligence system by studying the human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Yeah, I think that's right. In the same way that to build flying machines, we want to understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: the laws of aerodynamics, including birds, but not mimic the birds. But they're the same laws.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: You have a view on AI, artificial intelligence, and safety that, from my perspective, is

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: refreshingly rational, or perhaps more importantly, has elements of positivity to it, which I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: can be inspiring and empowering as opposed to paralyzing. For many people, including AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: researchers, the eventual existential threat of AI is obvious. Not only possible, but obvious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: And for many others, including AI researchers, the threat is not obvious. Elon Musk is famously

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: in the highly concerned about AI camp, saying things like AI is far more dangerous than nuclear

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: weapons, and that AI will likely destroy human civilization. So in February, he said that if Elon

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: was really serious about AI, the threat of AI, he would stop building self-driving cars that he's

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: doing very successfully as part of Tesla. Then he said, wow, if even Pinker doesn't understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: the difference between narrow AI, like a car, and general AI, when the latter literally has a million

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: times more compute power and an open-ended utility function, humanity is in deep trouble.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: So first, what did you mean by the statement about Elon Musk should stop building self-driving cars

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: if he's deeply concerned?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Not the last time that Elon Musk has fired off an intemperate tweet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Well, we live in a world where Twitter has power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Yes. Yeah, I think there are two kinds of existential threat that have been discussed

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: in connection with artificial intelligence, and I think that they're both incoherent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: One of them is a vague fear of AI takeover, that just as we subjugated animals and less

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: technologically advanced peoples, so if we build something that's more advanced than us,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: it will inevitably turn us into pets or slaves or domesticated animal equivalents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: I think this confuses intelligence with a will to power, that it so happens that in the intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: system we are most familiar with, namely homo sapiens, we are products of natural selection,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: which is a competitive process, and so bundled together with our problem-solving capacity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: are a number of nasty traits like dominance and exploitation and maximization of power

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: and glory and resources and influence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: There's no reason to think that sheer problem-solving capability will set that as one of its goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Its goals will be whatever we set its goals as, and as long as someone isn't building a

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: megalomaniacal artificial intelligence, then there's no reason to think that it would naturally

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: evolve in that direction. Now, you might say, well, what if we gave it the goal of

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: maximizing its own power source? Well, that's a pretty stupid goal to give an autonomous system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: You don't give it that goal. I mean, that's just self-evidently idiotic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: So if you look at the history of the world, there's been a lot of opportunities where engineers

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: could instill in a system destructive power, and they choose not to because that's the

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: natural process of engineering. Well, except for weapons. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: if you're building a weapon, its goal is to destroy people, and so I think there are good

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: reasons to not build certain kinds of weapons. I think building nuclear weapons was a massive mistake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: You do. You think... So maybe pause on that because that is one of the serious threats.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Do you think that it was a mistake in a sense that it should have been stopped early on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: or do you think it's just an unfortunate event of invention that this was invented?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Do you think it was possible to stop, I guess is the question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: It's hard to rewind the clock because, of course, it was invented in the context of World War II

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: and the fear that the Nazis might develop one first. Then once it was initiated for that reason,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: it was hard to turn off, especially since winning the war against the Japanese and the Nazis was

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: such an overwhelming goal of every responsible person that there's just nothing that people

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: wouldn't have done then to ensure victory. It's quite possible if World War II hadn't happened

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: that nuclear weapons wouldn't have been invented. We can't know, but I don't think it was by any

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: means a necessity, any more than some of the other weapon systems that were envisioned but never

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: implemented, like planes that would disperse poison gas over cities like crop dusters or systems to

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: create earthquakes and tsunamis in enemy countries, to weaponize the weather, weaponize solar flares,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: all kinds of crazy schemes that we thought the better of. I think analogies between nuclear

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: weapons and artificial intelligence are fundamentally misguided because the whole point of nuclear

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: weapons is to destroy things. The point of artificial intelligence is not to destroy things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: The analogy is misleading. There's two artificial intelligence you mentioned. The first one, I guess,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: highly intelligent or power hungry. Yeah, an assistant that we design ourselves where we give

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: it the goals. Goals are external to the means to attain the goals. If we don't design an

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: artificial intelligence system to maximize dominance, then it won't maximize dominance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: It's just that we're so familiar with homo sapiens where these two traits come bundled together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: particularly in men, that we are apt to confuse high intelligence with a will to power,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: but that's just an error. The other fear is that will be collateral damage that will give

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: artificial intelligence a goal like make paper clips, and it will pursue that goal so brilliantly

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: that before we can stop it, it turns us into paper clips. We'll give it the goal of curing cancer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: and it will turn us into guinea pigs for lethal experiments, or give it the goal of world peace,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: and its conception of world peace is no people, therefore no fighting, and so it will kill us all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Now, I think these are utterly fanciful. In fact, I think they're actually self-defeating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: They, first of all, assume that we're going to be so brilliant that we can design an artificial

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: intelligence that can cure cancer, but so stupid that we don't specify what we mean by curing cancer

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: in enough detail that it won't kill us in the process, and it assumes that the system will be

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: so smart that it can cure cancer, but so idiotic that it can't figure out that what we mean by

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: curing cancer is not killing everyone. So I think that the collateral damage scenario,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: the value alignment problem, is also based on a misconception.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: So one of the challenges, of course, we don't know how to build either system currently,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: or are we even close to knowing. Of course, those things can change overnight, but at this time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: theorizing about it is very challenging in either direction. So that's probably at the core of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: problem is without that ability to reason about the real engineering things here at hand,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: is your imagination runs away with things. But let me sort of ask, what do you think was the

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: motivation and the thought process of Elon Musk? I build autonomous vehicles, I study autonomous

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: vehicles, I study Tesla autopilot. I think it is one of the greatest currently application,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: large-scale application of artificial intelligence in the world. It has potentially a very positive

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: impact on society. So how does a person who's creating this very good, quote unquote, narrow AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: system also seem to be so concerned about this other general AI? What do you think is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: motivation there? What do you think is the thing? Well, you probably have to ask him, but there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: and he is notoriously flamboyant, impulsive, as we have just seen, to the detriment of his own goals

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: of the health of a company. So I don't know what's going on in his mind. You'd probably have to ask

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: him. But I don't think the distinction between special purpose AI and so-called general AI is

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: relevant, that in the same way that special purpose AI is not going to do anything conceivable in

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: order to attain a goal. All engineering systems are designed to trade off across multiple goals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: When we built cars in the first place, we didn't forget to install brakes because the goal of a

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: car is to go fast. It occurred to people, yes, you want it to go fast, but not always. So you

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: would build in brakes too. Likewise, if a car is going to be autonomous and program it to take the

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: shortest route to the airport, it's not going to take the diagonal and mow down people and trees

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: and fences because that's the shortest route. That's not what we mean by the shortest route when we

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: program it. And that's just what an intelligence system is by definition. It takes into account

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: multiple constraints. The same is true, in fact, even more true of so-called general intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: That is, if it's genuinely intelligent, it's not going to pursue some goal single-mindedly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: omitting every other consideration and collateral effect. That's not artificial

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: and general intelligence. That's artificial stupidity. I agree with you, by the way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: on the promise of autonomous vehicles for improving human welfare. I think it's spectacular.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: And I'm surprised at how little press coverage notes that in the United States alone, something

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: like 40,000 people die every year on the highways, vastly more than are killed by terrorists. And we

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: spend a trillion dollars on a war to combat deaths by terrorism, about half a dozen a year,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: whereas year in, year out, 40,000 people are massacred on the highways, which could be brought

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: down to very close to zero. So I'm with you on the humanitarian benefit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Let me just mention that as a person who's building these cars, it is a little bit offensive to me to

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: say that engineers would be clueless enough not to engineer safety into systems. I often stay up at

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: night thinking about those 40,000 people that are dying. And everything I try to engineer is to save

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: those people's lives. So every new invention that I'm super excited about, every new,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: in all the deep learning literature and CVPR conferences and NIPS, everything I'm super excited

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: about is all grounded in making it safe and help people. So I just don't see how that trajectory

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: can all of a sudden slip into a situation where intelligence will be highly negative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: You and I, you and I certainly agree on that. And I think that's only the beginning of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: potential humanitarian benefits of artificial intelligence. There's been enormous attention to

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: what are we going to do with the people whose jobs are made obsolete by artificial intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: but very little attention given to the fact that the jobs that are going to be made obsolete are

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: horrible jobs. The fact that people aren't going to be picking crops and making beds and driving

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: trucks and mining coal, these are soul deadening jobs. And we have a whole literature sympathizing

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: with the people stuck in these menial, mind deadening, dangerous jobs. If we can eliminate

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: them, this is a fantastic boon to humanity. Now granted, you solve one problem and there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: another one, namely how do we get these people a decent income? But if we're smart enough to

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: invent machines that can make beds and put away dishes and handle hospital patients,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: well, I think we're smart enough to figure out how to redistribute income to

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: portion some of the vast economic savings to the human beings who will no longer be needed to make

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: beds. Okay. Sam Harris says that it's obvious that eventually AI will be an existential risk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: He's one of the people who says it's obvious. We don't know when the claim goes, but eventually

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: it's obvious. And because we don't know when we should worry about it now. It's a very interesting

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: argument in my eyes. So how do we think about time scale? How do we think about existential threats

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: when we don't really, we know so little about the threat, unlike nuclear weapons, perhaps,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: about this particular threat, that it could happen tomorrow, right? So, but very likely won't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Yeah. They're likely to be a hundred years away. So how do, do we ignore it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Do, how do we talk about it? Do we worry about it? What, how do we think about those?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: What is it? A threat that we can imagine. It's within the limits of our imagination,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: but not within our limits of understanding to sufficient to accurately predict it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: But what, what is, what is the it that we're afraid of?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Oh, AI, sorry. AI, AI being the existential threat. AI can always-

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: But how? Will it be like enslaving us or turning us into paper clips?

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: I think the most compelling from the Sam Harris perspective would be the paper clip situation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: Yeah. I mean, I just think it's totally fanciful. I mean, don't build a system. Don't give it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: don't, first of all, the code of engineering is you don't implement a system with massive control

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: before testing it. Now, perhaps the culture of engineering will radically change. Then I would

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: worry, but I don't see any signs that engineers will suddenly do idiotic things like put a,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: uh, an electrical power plant in control of a system that they haven't tested, uh, first,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: uh, or all of these scenarios, not only imagine a, um, almost a magically powered intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: you know, including things like cure cancer, which is probably an incoherent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: goal because there's so many different kinds of cancer, uh, or bring about world peace.

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: I mean, how do you even specify that as a goal? But the scenario is also imagine some degree of

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: control of every molecule in the universe, uh, which not only is itself unlikely, but we would

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: not start to connect these systems to, uh, infrastructure without, uh, without, um, testing

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: as we would any kind of engineering system. Now, maybe some engineers will be irresponsible and we

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: need legal and, um, uh, regulatory and, uh, legal responsibility implemented so that engineers don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: do things that are stupid by their own standards. But the, uh, uh, I, I've never seen enough of a

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: plausible scenario of, uh, existential threat to devote large amounts of brain power to, to forestall

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: it. So you believe in the sort of the power on mass of the engineering of real world, uh,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: of reason as you argue in your latest book of reason and science to sort of be the very thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: that guides the development of new technology. So it's safe and also keeps us safe. Yeah. It's the

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: same, you know, granted the same culture of safety that currently is part of the engineering, uh,

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

body.input: mindset for airplanes, for example. So yeah, I don't think that, that, uh, that that should be

metadata.title: Podcast: Steven Pinker: AI in the Age of Reason | Lex Fridman Podcast #3

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: For example, it turns out one of the hardest problems we had was when helicopters flying around upside down doing stunts,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: how do you figure out the position? How do you localize a helicopter?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So we wanted to try all sorts of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Having one GPS unit doesn't work because you're flying upside down, GPS units facing down, so you can't see the satellites.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So we tried, we experimented trying to have two GPS units, one facing up, one facing down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So if you flip over, that didn't work because the downward facing one couldn't synchronize if you're flipping quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Morgan Quigley was exploring this crazy complicated configuration of specialized hardware to interpret GPS signals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Looking at FPG is completely insane.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Spent about a year working on that, didn't work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I remember Peter, great guy, him and me, sitting down in my office,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: looking at some of the latest things we had tried that didn't work and saying, you know, done it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Like what now? Because we tried so many things and it just didn't work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: In the end, what we did, and Adam Coles was crucial to this, was put cameras on the ground

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: and use cameras on the ground to localize the helicopter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And that solved the localization problem so that we could then focus on the reinforcement learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: and inverse reinforcement learning techniques to then actually make the helicopter fly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And, you know, I'm reminded when I was doing this work at Stanford around that time,
