metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: there was a lot of reinforcement learning theoretical papers, but not a lot of practical applications.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So the autonomous helicopter work for flying helicopters was one of the few practical applications

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: of reinforcement learning at the time, which caused it to become pretty well known.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I feel like we might have almost come full circle with today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: There's so much buzz, so much hype, so much excitement about reinforcement learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But again, we're hunting for more applications of all of these great ideas that the communities come up with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: What was the drive sort of in the face of the fact that most people are doing theoretical work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: What motivate you in the uncertainty and the challenges to get the helicopter sort of to do the applied work,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: to get the actual system to work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah, in the face of fear, uncertainty, sort of the setbacks that you mentioned for localization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I like stuff that works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: In the physical world. So like it's back to the shredder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You know, I like theory, but when I work on theory myself, and this is personal taste,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I'm not saying anyone else should do what I do, but when I work on theory, I personally enjoy it more

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: if I feel that the work I do will influence people, have positive impact, will help someone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I remember when many years ago I was speaking with a mathematics professor, and it kind of just said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: hey, why do you do what you do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And he said, he had stars in his eyes when he answered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And this mathematician, not from Stanford, different university, he said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I do what I do because it helps me to discover truth and beauty in the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: He had stars in his eyes, he said. And I thought that's great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I don't want to do that. I think it's great that someone does that, fully support the people that do it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: a lot of respect for people that, but I am more motivated when I can see a line to how the work that my teams

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: and I are doing helps people. The world needs all sorts of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I'm just one type. I don't think everyone should do things the same way as I do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But when I delve into either theory or practice, if I personally have conviction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: that here's a pathway to help people, I find that more satisfying to have that conviction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That's your path. You were a proponent of deep learning before it gained widespread acceptance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: What did you see in this field that gave you confidence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: What was your thinking process like in that first decade of the, I don't know what that's called, 2000s, the aughts?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah, I can tell you the thing we got wrong and the thing we got right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: The thing we really got wrong was the importance of, the early importance of unsupervised learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So early days of Google Brain, we put a lot of effort into unsupervised learning rather than supervised learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And there was this argument, I think it was around 2005 after NeurIPS at that time called NIPS, but now NeurIPS had ended.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And Jeff Finton and I were sitting in the cafeteria outside the conference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: We had lunch, we were just chatting. And Jeff pulled up this napkin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: He started sketching this argument on a napkin. It was very compelling as I repeated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Human brain has about 100 trillion, so there's 10 to the 14 synaptic connections.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You will live for about 10 to the nine seconds. That's 30 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You actually live for two by 10 to the nine, maybe three by 10 to the nine seconds. So just let's say 10 to the nine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So if each synaptic connection, each weight in your brain's neural network has just a one bit parameter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: that's 10 to the 14 bits you need to learn in up to 10 to the nine seconds of your life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So by this simple argument, which is a lot of problems, it's very simplified, that's 10 to the five bits per second you need to learn in your life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I have a one year old daughter. I am not pointing out 10 to five bits per second of labels to her.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So, and I think I'm a very loving parent, but I'm just not going to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So from this very crude, definitely problematic argument, there's just no way that most of what we know is through supervised learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But where you get so many bits of information is from sucking in images, audio, just experiences in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And so that argument, and there are a lot of known flaws in this argument, which we should go into, really convinced me that there's a lot of power to unsupervised learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So that was the part that we actually maybe got wrong. I still think unsupervised learning is really important, but in the early days, 10, 15 years ago, a lot of us thought that was the path forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Oh, so you're saying that that perhaps was the wrong intuition for the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: For the time. That was the part we got wrong. The part we got right was the importance of scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So Adam Coates, another wonderful person, fortunate to have worked with him. He was in my group at Stanford at the time, and Adam had run these experiments at Stanford, showing that the bigger we train a learning algorithm, the better its performance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And it was based on that, there was a graph that Adam generated, where the X axis, Y axis lines going up into the right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So the bigger you make this thing, the better its performance, accuracy is the vertical axis. So it's really based on that chart that Adam generated that gave me the conviction that you could scale these models way bigger than what we could on a few CPUs, which is where we had a Stanford, that we could get even better results.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And it was really based on that one figure that Adam generated that gave me the conviction to go with Sebastian Thrun to pitch, you know, starting a project at Google, which became the Google Brain project.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And you go find Google Brain, and there the intuition was scale will bring performance for the system. So we should chase larger and larger scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I think people don't realize how groundbreaking of a, it's simple, but it's a groundbreaking idea that bigger datasets will result in better performance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It was controversial at the time. Some of my well-meaning friends, senior people in the machine learning community, I won't name, but some of whom we know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: My well-meaning friends came and were trying to give me friendly advice. Hey, Andrew, why are you doing this? This is crazy. It's in the neural network architecture. Look at these architectures of building.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You just want to go for scale? Like this is a bad career move. So my well-meaning friends, you know, we're trying to, some of them were trying to talk me out of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But I find that if you want to make a breakthrough, you sometimes have to have conviction and do something before it's popular, since that lets you have a bigger impact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Let me ask you just in a small tangent on that topic. I find myself arguing with people saying that greater scale, especially in the context of active learning, so very carefully selecting the dataset,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: growing the scale of the dataset is going to lead to even further breakthroughs in deep learning. And there's currently pushback at that idea that larger datasets are no longer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So you want to increase the efficiency of learning. You want to make better learning mechanisms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I personally believe that bigger datasets will still, with the same learning methods we have now, will result in better performance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: What's your intuition at this time on those, on the dual side? Do we need to come up with better architectures for learning or can we just get bigger, better datasets that will improve performance?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think both are important. And it's also problem dependent. So for a few datasets, we may be approaching, you know, base error rate or approaching or surpassing human level performance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And then there's that theoretical ceiling that we will never surpass, so base error rate. But then I think there are plenty of problems where we're still quite far from either human level performance or from base error rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And bigger datasets with neural networks without further algorithmic innovation will be sufficient to take us further.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But on the flip side, if we look at the recent breakthroughs using your transforming networks for language models, it was a combination of novel architecture, but also scale had a lot to do with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: If we look at what happened with GP2 and BERT, I think scale was a large part of the story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah, that's not often talked about is the scale of the dataset it was trained on and the quality of the dataset because there's some redded threads that were uprated highly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So there's already some weak supervision on a very large dataset that people don't often talk about, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I find that today we have maturing processes to managing code, things like Git, right? Version control. It took us a long time to evolve the good processes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I remember when my friends and I were emailing each other C++ files and email, you know, but then we had was it CVS subversion, Git, maybe something else in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: We're very immature in terms of tools for managing data and think about the clean data and how to solve very hot, messy data problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think there's a lot of innovation there to be had still.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I love the idea that you were versioning through email.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I'll give you one example. When we work with manufacturing companies, it's not at all uncommon for there to be multiple labelists that disagree with each other, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And so we would do the work in visual inspection. We will take, say, a plastic part and show it to one inspector. And the inspector, sometimes very opinionated, they'll go, clearly that's a defect, this scratch, unacceptable, got to reject this part.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Take the same part to a different inspector, different, very opinionated, clearly the scratch is small, it's fine, don't throw it away, you're going to make us, you know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And then sometimes you take the same plastic part, show it to the same inspector in the afternoon and expose in the morning and very opinionated go in the morning to say, clearly it's okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: In the afternoon, equally confident, clearly this is a defect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And so what is the AI team supposed to do if sometimes even one person doesn't agree with himself or herself in the span of a day?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think these are the types of very practical, very messy data problems that my teams wrestle with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: In the case of large consumer internet companies where you have a billion users, you have a lot of data, you don't worry about it, just take the average, it kind of works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But in a case of other industry settings, we don't have big data, if it's a small data, very small data sets, maybe around 100 defective parts or 100 examples of a defect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: If you have only 100 examples, these little labeling errors, you know, if 10 of your 100 labels are wrong, that actually is 10% of your data set has a big impact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So how do you clean this up? What are you supposed to do? This is an example of the types of things that my teams, this is a landing AI example, are wrestling with to deal with small data, which comes up all the time once you're outside consumer internet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah, that's fascinating. So then you invest more effort and time in thinking about the actual labeling process. What are the labels? What are the how are disagreements resolved and all those kinds of like pragmatic real world problems? That's a fascinating space.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah, I find it actually when I'm teaching at Stanford, I increasingly encourage students at Stanford to try to find their own project for the end of term project rather than just downloading someone else's nicely clean data set.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's actually much harder if you need to go and define your own problem and find your own data set rather than you go to one of the several good websites, very good websites with with clean scopes data sets that you could just work on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You're not running three efforts that AI fund landing AI and deep learning dot AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: As you've said, the AI fund is involved in creating new companies from scratch landing AI is involved in helping already established companies do AI and deep learning AI is for education of everyone else or of individuals interested in of getting into the field and excelling in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So let's perhaps talk about each of these areas. First, deep learning dot AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: How the basic question, how does a person interested in deep learning get started in the field.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Deep learning AI is working to create causes to help people break into AI. So my machine learning course that I taught through Stanford means one of the most popular causes on Coursera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: To this day, it's probably one of the courses, sort of, if I ask somebody, how did you get into machine learning or how did you fall in love with machine learning or get you interested.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It always goes back to and rang at some point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So you've been flowing the amount of people you've influenced is ridiculous. So for that, I'm sure I speak for a lot of people say big thank you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: No, yeah, thank you. You know, I was once once reading a news article. I think it was tech review and I'm going to mess up the statistic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But I remember reading an article that said something like one third of all programmers are self taught.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I may have the number one third of all, it was two thirds. But when I read the article, I thought this doesn't make sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Everyone is self taught. So because you teach yourself. I don't teach people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That's well put. So yeah. So how does one get started in deep learning and where does deep learning that I fit into that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So the deep learning specialization offered by D.V.M.A.I. is I think one was Coursera's top specialization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It might still be. So it's a very popular way for people to take that specialization, to learn about everything from neural networks to how to tune in your network.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: To what is a conf net to what is a R.N.N. or a sequence model or what is an attention model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And so the deep learning specialization steps every once through those algorithms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So you deeply understand it and can implement it and use it for whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: From the very beginning. So what would you say are the prerequisites for somebody to take the deep learning specialization in terms of maybe math or programming background?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah. Need to understand basic programming since there are programming exercises in Python and the math pre-rec is quite basic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So no calculus is needed. If you know calculus is great, you get better intuitions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But deliberately try to teach that specialization without requiring calculus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think high school math would be sufficient if you know how to multiply two matrices. I think that that's that that's great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So a little basic linear algebra is great. Basically algebra, even very, very basic linear algebra in some programming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think that people that have done the machine learning course will find the deep learning specialization a bit easier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But it's also possible to jump into the deep learning specialization directly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But it will be a little bit harder since we tend to go over faster concepts like how does gradient descent work and what is the objective function, which covered more slowly in the machine learning course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Could you briefly mention some of the key concepts in deep learning that students should learn that you envision them learning in the first few months in the first year or so?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So if you take the deep learning specialization, you learn the foundations of what is a neural network.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: How do you build up a neural network from a single logistic unit, stack of layers to different activation functions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You learn how to train the neural networks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: One thing I'm very proud of in that specialization is we go through a lot of practical know how of how to actually make these things work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So what are the differences between different optimization algorithms? What do you do if the algorithm overfits?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So how do you tell if the algorithm is overfitting? When do you collect more data? When should you not bother to collect more data?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I find that even today, unfortunately, there are engineers that will spend six months trying to pursue a particular direction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: such as collect more data because we heard more data is valuable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But sometimes you could run some tests and could have figured out six months earlier that for this particular problem, collecting more data isn't going to cut it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So just don't spend six months collecting more data. Spend your time modifying the architecture or trying something else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So go through a lot of the practical know how so that when someone, when you take the deep learning specialization,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: you have those skills to be very efficient in how you build these networks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So dive right in to play with the network, to train it, to do the inference on a particular data set,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: to build an intuition about it without without building it up too big to where you spend, like you said, six months learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: building up your big project without building any intuition of a small small aspect of the data that could already tell you everything you need to know about that data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yes. And also the systematic frameworks of thinking for how to go about building practical machine learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Maybe to make an analogy, when we learn to code, we have to learn the syntax of some programming language, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Be it Python or C++ or Octave or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But that equally important or maybe even more important part of coding is to understand how to string together these lines of code into coherent things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So, you know, when should you put something in a function column? When should you not? How do you think about abstraction?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So those frameworks are what makes a programmer efficient, even more than understanding the syntax.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I remember when I was an undergrad at Carnegie Mellon, one of my friends would debug their code by first trying to compile it and then C++ code.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And then every line did a syntax error. They want to get rid of the syntax errors as quickly as possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So how do you do that? Well, they would delete every single line of code with a syntax error.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So really efficient for getting rid of syntax errors for horrible debugging errors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think so we learn how to debug. And I think in machine learning, the way you debug a machine learning program is very different than the way you do binary search or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Use a debugger, trace through the code in traditional software engineering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So it's an evolving discipline.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But I find that the people that are really good at debugging machine learning algorithms are easily 10x, maybe 100x faster at getting something to work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And the basic process of debugging is the bug in this case. Why isn't this thing learning, improving, sort of going into the questions of overfitting and all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That's the logical space that the debugging is happening in with neural networks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah. The often the question is, why doesn't it work yet?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Or can I expect it to eventually work? And what are the things I could try? Change the architecture, more data, more regularization, different optimization algorithm, different types of data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So to answer those questions systematically so that you don't spend six months hitting down the blind alley before someone comes and says, why did you spend six months doing this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: What concepts in deep learning do you think students struggle the most with or sort of is the biggest challenge for them wants to get over that hill?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's it hooks them and it inspires them and they really get it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Similar to learning mathematics, I think one of the challenges of deep learning is that there are a lot of concepts that build on top of each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: If you ask me what's hard about mathematics, I have a hard time pinpointing one thing. Is it addition, subtraction? Is it a carry? Is it multiplication? There's just a lot of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think one of the challenges of learning math and of learning certain technical fields is that there are a lot of concepts and if you miss a concept, then you're kind of missing the prerequisite for something that comes later.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So in the deep learning specialization, try to break down the concepts to maximize the odds of each component being understandable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So when you move on to the more advanced thing, we learn we have confidence, hopefully you have enough intuitions from the earlier sections to then understand why we structure confidence in a certain way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And then eventually why we built RNNs and LSTMs or attention models in a certain way, building on top of the earlier concepts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Actually, I'm curious, you do a lot of teaching as well. Do you have a favorite, this is the hard concept moment in your teaching?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Well, I don't think anyone's ever turned the interview on me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Glad to hear that first.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think that's a really good question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah, it's really hard to capture the moment when they struggle. I think you put it really eloquently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I do think there's moments that are like aha moments that really inspire people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think for some reason, reinforcement learning, especially deep reinforcement learning, is a really great way to really inspire people and get what the use of neural networks can do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Even though neural networks really are just a part of the deep RL framework, but it's a really nice way to paint the entirety of the picture of a neural network being able to learn from scratch, knowing nothing and explore the world and pick up lessons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I find that a lot of the aha moments happen when you use deep RL to teach people about neural networks, which is counterintuitive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I find like a lot of the inspired sort of fire in people's passion, people's eyes, it comes from the RL world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Do you find reinforcement learning to be a useful part of the teaching process or no?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I still teach reinforcement learning in one of my Stanford classes and my PhD thesis was on reinforcement learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I find that if I'm trying to teach students the most useful techniques for them to use today, I end up shrinking the amount of time I talk about reinforcement learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's not what's working today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Now our world changes so fast, maybe it does be totally different in a couple of years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But I think we need a couple more things for reinforcement learning to get there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: One of my teams is looking to reinforcement learning for some robotic control tasks. So I see the applications, but if you look at it as a percentage of all of the impact of the types of things we do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: at least today, outside of playing video games, right, in a few of the games, the scope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Actually, at Neurobe, a bunch of us were standing around saying, hey, what's your best example of an actual deploy reinforcement learning application among senior machine learning researchers?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And again, there are some emerging ones, but there are not that many great examples.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think you're absolutely right. The sad thing is there hasn't been a big impact for real world application reinforcement learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think its biggest impact to me has been in the toy domain, in the game domain, in the small example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That's what I mean for educational purposes. It seems to be a fun thing to explore neural networks with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But I think from your perspective, and I think that might be the best perspective, is if you're trying to educate with a simple example in order to illustrate how this can actually be grown to scale and have a real world impact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: then perhaps focusing on the fundamentals of supervised learning in the context of a simple data set, even like an MNIST data set, is the right way, is the right path to take.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: The amount of fun I've seen people have with reinforcement learning has been great, but not in the applied impact on the real world setting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So it's a trade off, how much impact you want to have versus how much fun you want to have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That's really cool. And I feel like the world actually needs all sorts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Even within machine learning, I feel like deep learning is so exciting, but the AI team shouldn't just use deep learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I find that my teams use a portfolio of tools, and maybe that's not the exciting thing to say, but some days we use a neural net, some days we use a PCA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Actually, the other day I was sitting down with my team looking at PCA residuals, trying to figure out what's going on with PCA applied to a manufacturing problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Some days we use a probabilistic graphical model. Some days we use a knowledge draft, which is one of the things that has tremendous industry impact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But the amount of chatter about knowledge drafts in academia is really thin compared to the actual rural impact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think reinforcement learning should be in that portfolio, and it's about balancing how much we teach all of these things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And the world should have diverse skills. It would be sad if everyone just learned one narrow thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah, the diverse skill helped you discover the right tool for the job.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: What is the most beautiful, surprising, or inspiring idea in deep learning to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Something that captivated your imagination. Is it the scale that could be achieved, the performance that could be achieved with scale, or is there other ideas?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think that if my only job was being an academic researcher, if I had an unlimited budget and didn't have to worry about short-term impact and only focus on long-term impact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I'd probably spend all my time doing research on unsupervised learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I still think unsupervised learning is a beautiful idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: At both this past New York and ICML, I was attending workshops or listening to various talks about self-supervised learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: which is one vertical segment, maybe, of unsupervised learning that I'm excited about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Maybe just to summarize the idea, I guess you know the idea I'll describe briefly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: No, please.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So here's an example of self-supervised learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Let's say we grab a lot of unlabeled images off the internet, so with infinite amounts of this type of data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I'm going to take each image and rotate it by a random multiple of 90 degrees.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And then I'm going to train a supervised neural network to predict what was the original orientation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So has this been rotated 90 degrees, 180 degrees, 270 degrees, or 0 degrees?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So you can generate an infinite amount of labeled data because you rotated the image so you know what's the ground truth label.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And so various researchers have found that by taking unlabeled data and making up labeled data sets and training a large neural network on these tasks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: you can then take the hidden layer representation and transfer it to a different task very powerfully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Learning word embeddings where we take a sentence, delete a word, predict the missing word, which is how we learn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: One of the ways we learn word embeddings is another example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I think there's now this portfolio of techniques for generating these made up tasks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Another one called Jigsaw would be if you take an image, cut it up into a 3x3 grid, so like a 9, 3x3 puzzle piece,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: jump out the 9 pieces and have a neural network predict which of the 9 factorial possible permutations it came from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So many groups, including OpenAI, Peter B has been doing some work on this too, Facebook, Google Brain, I think DeepMind,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Aaron VanderAald has great work on the CPC objective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So many teams are doing exciting work and I think this is a way to generate infinite labeled data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I find this a very exciting piece of unsuai-san.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So long term you think that's going to unlock a lot of power in machine learning systems?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Is this kind of unsupervised learning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I don't think there's a whole enchilada. I think it's just a piece of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I think this one piece, self-supervised learning, is starting to get traction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: We're very close to it being useful. Well, word embeddings are really useful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think we're getting closer and closer to just having a significant real-world impact, maybe in computer vision and video.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But I think this concept, and I think there'll be other concepts around it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Other unsupervised learning things that I worked on, I've been excited about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I was really excited about sparse coding and ICA, slow feature analysis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think all of these are ideas that various of us were working on about a decade ago before we all got distracted by how well supervised learning was doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So we would return to the fundamentals of representation learning that really started this movement of deep learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think there's a lot more work that one could explore around this theme of ideas and other ideas to come up with better algorithms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So if we could return to maybe talk quickly about the specifics of deeplearning.ai, the deep learning specialization perhaps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: How long does it take to complete the course, would you say?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: The official length of the deep learning specialization is I think 16 weeks, so about four months, but it's got your own pace.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So if you subscribe to the deep learning specialization, there are people that finish it in less than a month by working more intensely and studying more intensely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So it really depends on the individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: When we created the deep learning specialization, we wanted to make it very accessible and very affordable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And with Coursera and deep learning.ai's education mission, one of the things that's really important to me is that if there's someone for whom paying anything is a financial hardship,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: then just apply for financial aid and get it for free.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: If you were to recommend a daily schedule for people in learning, whether it's through the deep learning.ai specialization or just learning in the world of deep learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: what would you recommend? How do they go about day to day, sort of specific advice about learning, about their journey in the world of deep learning, machine learning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think getting the habit of learning is key, and that means regularity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So for example, we send out our weekly newsletter, The Batch, every Wednesday.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So people know it's coming Wednesday, you can spend a little bit of time on Wednesday catching up on the latest news through The Batch on Wednesday.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And for myself, I've picked up a habit of spending some time every Saturday and every Sunday reading or studying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And so I don't wake up on a Saturday and have to make a decision.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Do I feel like reading or studying today or not? It's just what I do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And the fact that the habit makes it easier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think if someone can get into that habit, it's like, you know, just like we brush our teeth every morning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I don't think about it. If I thought about it, it's a little bit annoying to have to spend two minutes doing that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But it's a habit that it takes no cognitive load.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But this would be so much harder if we have to make a decision every morning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So and actually, that's the reason why I wear the same thing every day as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's just one less decision. I just get up and wear my blue shirt.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think if you can get that habit, that consistency of studying, then then actually feels easier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So yeah, it's kind of amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: In my own life, like I play guitar every day for the efforts myself to at least for five minutes play guitar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's a ridiculously short period of time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But because I've gotten into that habit, it's incredible what you can accomplish in a period of a year or two years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You can become, you know, exceptionally good at certain aspects of a thing by just doing it every day for a very short period of time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's kind of a miracle that that's how it works. It adds up over time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah, and I think it's often not about the burst of sustained efforts and the all-nighters,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: because you could only do that a limited number of times. It's the sustained effort over a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think, you know, reading two research papers is a nice thing to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But the power is not reading two research papers. It's reading two research papers a week for a year.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Then you read a hundred papers and you actually learn a lot when you read a hundred papers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So regularity and making learning a habit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Do you have general other study tips for particularly deep learning that people should,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: in their process of learning, is there some kind of recommendations or tips you have as they learn?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: One thing I still do when I'm trying to study something really deeply is take handwritten notes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It varies. I know there are a lot of people that take the deep learning courses during a commute or something where it may be more awkward to take notes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I know it may not work for everyone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But when I'm taking courses on Coursera, you know, and I still take some every now and then,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: the most recent one I took was a course on clinical trials because I was interested in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I got out my little Moleskine notebook and I was sitting in my desk just taking down notes of what the instructor was saying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And we know that that act of taking notes, preferably handwritten notes, increases retention.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So as you're sort of watching the video, just kind of pausing maybe and then taking the basic insights down on paper?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah. So there have been a few studies. If you search online, you find some of these studies that taking handwritten notes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: because handwriting is slower as we're saying just now, it causes you to recode the knowledge in your own words more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And that process of recoding promotes long term retention. This is as opposed to typing, which is fine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Again, typing is better than nothing. And taking a class and not taking notes is better than not taking any classes at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But comparing handwritten notes and typing, you can usually type faster for a lot of people than you can handwrite notes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And so when people type, they're more likely to just transcribe verbatim what they heard and that reduces the amount of recoding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And that actually results in less long term retention.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I don't know what the psychological effect there is, but it's so true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: There's something fundamentally different about handwriting. I wonder what that is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I wonder if it is as simple as just the time it takes to write is slower.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah. And because you can't write as many words, you have to take whatever they said and summarize it into a few words.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And that summarization process requires deeper processing of the meaning, which then results in better retention.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That's fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I think because of Coursera, I spent so much time studying pedagogy. It's actually one of my passions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I really love learning how to more efficiently help others learn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah. One of the things I do both in creating videos or when we write the batch is I try to think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: is one minute spent with us going to be a more efficient learning experience than one minute spent anywhere else?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And we really try to make it time efficient for the learners because everyone's busy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So when we're editing, I often tell my teams, every word needs to fight for its life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And if we can delete a word, that's not waste the learners time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's so amazing that you think that way because there is millions of people that are impacted by your teaching.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And that one minute spent has a ripple effect through years of time, which is fascinating to think about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: How does one make a career out of an interest in deep learning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Do you have advice for people? We just talked about the beginning, early steps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But if you want to make it an entire life's journey, or at least a journey of a decade or two, how do you do it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So most important thing is to get started.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I think in the early parts of a career, coursework like the deep learning specialization is a very efficient way to master this material.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So because instructors, be it me or someone else or Lawrence Maroney, who teaches intensive law specialization or other things we're working on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: spend effort to try to make it time efficient for you to learn new concepts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So coursework is actually a very efficient way for people to learn concepts in the beginning parts of breaking into new fields.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: In fact, one thing I see at Stanford, some of my PhD students want to jump into research right away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I actually tend to say, look, in your first couple years of PhD, you didn't spend time taking courses because it lays the foundation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's fine if you're less productive in your first couple of years, you'll be better off in the long term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Beyond a certain point, there's materials that doesn't exist in courses because it's too cutting edge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: The courses haven't been created yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: There's some practical experience that we're not yet that good as teaching in a course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I think after exhausting the efficient coursework, then most people need to go on to either ideally work on projects

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: and then maybe also continue their learning by reading blog posts and research papers and things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Doing projects is really important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And again, I think it's important to start small and just do something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Today you read about deep learning, it feels like, oh, all these people are doing such exciting things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: What if I'm not building a neural network that changes the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And what's the point?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Well, the point is sometimes building that tiny neural network, you know, be it MNIST or upgrade to a fashion MNIST, to whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So doing your own fun hobby project.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That's how you gain the skills to let you do bigger and bigger projects.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I find this to be true at the individual level and also at the organizational level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: For a company to become good at machine learning, sometimes the right thing to do is not to tackle the giant project,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: it's instead to do the small project that lets the organization learn and then build out from there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But this is true both for individuals and for companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Taking the first step and then taking small steps is the key.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Should students pursue a PhD?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Do you think you can do so much?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That's one of the fascinating things in machine learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You can have so much impact without ever getting a PhD.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So what are your thoughts?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Should people go to grad school? Should people get a PhD?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think that there are multiple good options of which doing a PhD could be one of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think that if someone's admitted to a top PhD program, you know, at MIT, Stanford, top schools,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think that's a very good experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Or if someone gets a job at a top organization, at the top AI team, I think that's also a very good experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: There are some things you still need a PhD to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: If someone's aspiration is to be a professor at the top academic university, you just need a PhD to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But if it goes to start a company, build a company, do great technical work, I think a PhD is a good experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73
