body.input: But I would look at the different options available to someone, you know, where are the places where you can get a job,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: where are the places you can get a PhD program, and kind of weigh the pros and cons of those.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So just to linger on that for a little bit longer, what final dreams and goals do you think people should have?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So what options should they explore?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So you can work in industry, so for a large company, like Google, Facebook, Baidu, all these large sort of companies

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: that already have huge teams of machine learning engineers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You can also do within industry sort of more research groups that kind of like Google research, Google Brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Then you can also do, like we said, a professor in academia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And what else? Oh, you can build your own company. You can do a startup.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Is there anything that stands out between those options or are they all beautiful different journeys that people should consider?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think the thing that affects your experience more is less, are you in this company versus that company or academia versus industry?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think the thing that affects your experience most is who are the people you're interacting with in a daily basis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So even if you look at some of the large companies, the experience of individuals in different teams is very different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And what matters most is not the logo above the door when you walk into the giant building every day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: What matters most is who are the 10 people, who are the 30 people you interact with every day?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I actually tend to advise people, if you get a job from a company, ask who is your manager,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: who are your peers, who are you actually going to talk to? We're all social creatures.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: We tend to become more like the people around us. And if you're working with great people, you will learn faster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Or if you get admitted, if you get a job at a great company or a great university, maybe the logo you walk in is great,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: but you're actually stuck on some team doing really work that doesn't excite you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And then that's actually a really bad experience. So this is true both for universities and for large companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: For small companies, you can kind of figure out who you'd be working with quite quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I tend to advise people if a company refuses to tell you who you work with, someone say, oh, join us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: If a rotation system will figure it out. I think that that's a worrying answer because it means you may not get sent to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: you may not actually get to a team with great peers and great people to work with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's actually a really profound advice that we kind of sometimes sweep. We don't consider too rigorously or carefully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: The people around you are really often, especially when you accomplish great things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: it seems that great things are accomplished because of the people around you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So that's a it's not about the the way whether you learn this thing or that thing, or like you said, the logo that hangs up top.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's the people. That's a fascinating and it's such a hard search process of finding just like finding the right friends

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: and somebody to get married with and that kind of thing. It's a very hard search. It's a people search problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah. But I think when someone interviews at a university or the research lab or the large corporation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: it's good to insist on just asking who are the people, who is my manager?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And if you refuse to tell me, I'm going to think, well, maybe that's because you don't have a good answer. It may not be someone I like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And if you don't particularly connect, if something feels off with the people, then don't stick to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That's a really important signal to consider.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah. And actually, in my Stanford class, CS230, as well as an ACM talk, I think I gave like an hour long talk on career advice,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: including on the job search process and some of these. So if you can find those videos online.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Awesome. And I'll point them. I'll point people to them. Beautiful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So the AI fund helps AI startups get off the ground, or perhaps you can elaborate on all the fun things it's involved with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: What's your advice on how does one build a successful AI startup?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You know, in Silicon Valley, a lot of startup failures come from building our products that no one wanted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So when, you know, cool technology, but who's going to use it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think I tend to be very outcome driven and customer obsessed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Ultimately, we don't get to vote if we succeed or fail. It's only the customer that the only one that gets a thumbs up or thumbs down vote in the long term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: In the short term, you know, there are various people that get various votes, but in the long term, that's what really matters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So as you build a startup, you have to constantly ask the question, will the customer give a thumbs up on this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think so. I think startups that are very customer focused, customer obsessed, deeply understand the customer and are oriented to serve the customer, are more likely to succeed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: With the provisional, I think all of us should only do things that we think create social good and moves the world forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I personally don't want to build addictive digital products just to sell a lot of ads.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: There are things that could be lucrative that I won't do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But if we can find ways to serve people in meaningful ways, I think those can be great things to do, either in the academic setting or in a corporate setting or a startup setting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So can you give me the idea of why you started the AI fund?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I remember when I was leading the AI group at Baidu, I had two jobs, two parts of my job.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: One was to build an AI engine to support the existing businesses and that was running, just ran, just performed by itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: The second part of my job at the time, which was to try to systematically initiate new lines of businesses using the company's AI capabilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So the self-driving car team came out of my group, the smart speaker team, similar to what is Amazon Echo Alexa in the US.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But we actually announced it before Amazon did, so Baidu wasn't following Amazon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That came out of my group and I found that to be actually the most fun part of my job.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So what I want to do was to build AI fund as a startup studio to systematically create new startups from scratch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: With all the things we can now do with AI, I think the ability to build new teams, to go after this rich space of opportunities is a very important mechanism to get these projects done that I think will move the world forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I've been fortunate to build a few teams that had a meaningful positive impact and I felt that we might be able to do this in a more systematic, repeatable way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So a startup studio is a relatively new concept.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: There are maybe dozens of startup studios right now, but I feel like all of us, many teams are still trying to figure out how do you systematically build companies with a high success rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think even a lot of my venture capital friends seem to be more and more building companies rather than investing in companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But I find it a fascinating thing to do to figure out the mechanisms by which we could systematically build successful teams, successful businesses in areas that we find meaningful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So a startup studio is a place and a mechanism for startups to go from zero to success, to try to develop a blueprint.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's actually a place for us to build startups from scratch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So we often bring in founders and work with them or maybe even have existing ideas that we match founders with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And then this launches, hopefully into successful companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So how close are you to figuring out a way to automate the process of starting from scratch and building a successful AI startup?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah, I think we've been constantly improving and iterating on our processes, how we do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So things like how many customer calls do we need to make and how do we get customer validation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: How do we make sure that this technology can be built?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Quite a lot of our businesses need cutting edge machine learning algorithms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So kind of algorithms have developed in the last one or two years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And even if it works in a research paper, it turns out taking the production is really hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: There are a lot of issues for making these things work in the real life that are not widely addressed in academia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So how do we validate that this is actually doable?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: How do we build a team, get the specialized domain knowledge, be it in education or healthcare or whatever sector we're focusing on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think we've actually been getting much better at giving the entrepreneurs a high success rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But I think the whole world is still in the early phases of figuring this out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Do you think there is some aspects of that process that are transferable from one startup to another, to another, to another?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah, very much so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Starting a company to most entrepreneurs is a really lonely thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I've seen so many entrepreneurs not know how to make certain decisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Like, when do you need to, how do you do B2B sales?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: If you don't know that, it's really hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Or how do you market this efficiently other than buying ads, which is really expensive?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Are there more efficient tactics to that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Or for a machine learning project, basic decisions can change the course of whether machine learning product works or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And so there are so many hundreds of decisions that entrepreneurs need to make.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And making a mistake in a couple key decisions can have a huge impact on the fate of the company.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think a startup studio provides a support structure that makes starting a company much less of a lonely experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And also, when facing with these key decisions, like trying to hire your first VP of engineering, what's a good selection criteria?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: How do you solve? Should I hire this person or not?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: By helping, by having an ecosystem around the entrepreneurs, the founders to help.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think we help them at the key moments and hopefully significantly make them more enjoyable and then higher success rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So they have somebody to brainstorm with in these very difficult decision points.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And also to help them recognize what they may not even realize is a key decision point.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That's the first and probably the most important part. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Actually, I can say one other thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think building companies is one thing, but I feel like it's really important that we build companies that move the world forward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: For example, within the AI Fund team, there was once an idea for a new company that if it had succeeded,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: would have resulted in people watching a lot more videos in a certain narrow vertical type of video.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I looked at it, the business case was fine, the revenue case was fine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But I looked and just said, I don't want to do this. I don't actually just want to have a lot more people watch this type of video.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It wasn't educational. It's an educational baby.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And so I co-ed the idea on the basis that I didn't think would actually help people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So whether building companies or work of enterprises or doing personal projects,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think it's up to each of us to figure out what's the difference we want to make in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: With Landing AI, you help already established companies grow their AI and machine learning efforts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: How does a large company integrate machine learning into their efforts?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: AI is a general purpose technology, and I think it will transform every industry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Our community has already transformed to a large extent the software internet sector.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Most software internet companies outside the top five or six or three or four already have reasonable machine learning capabilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Or getting there is still room for improvement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But when I look outside the software internet sector, everything from manufacturing, agriculture, health care, logistics, transportation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: there's so many opportunities that very few people are working on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think the next wave for AI is for us to also transform all of those other industries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: There was a McKinsey study estimating $13 trillion of global economic growth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: US GDP is $19 trillion, so $13 trillion is a big number.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Or PWC estimates $16 trillion. So whatever number is, is large.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But the interesting thing to me was a lot of that impact would be outside the software internet sector.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So we need more teams to work with these companies to help them adopt AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I think this is one thing that will help drive global economic growth and make humanity more powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And like you said, the impact is there. So what are the best industries, the biggest industries where AI can help, perhaps outside the software tech sector?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Frankly, I think it's all of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Some of the ones I'm spending a lot of time on are manufacturing, agriculture, looking to health care.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: For example, in manufacturing, we do a lot of work in visual inspection,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: where today there are people standing around using the human eye to check if this plastic part or the smartphone or this thing has a scratch or a dent or something in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: We can use a camera to take a picture, use a algorithm, deep learning and other things to check if it's defective or not,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: and thus help factories improve yield and improve quality and improve throughput.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It turns out the practical problems we run into are very different than the ones you might read about in most research papers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: The data sets are really small, so we face small data problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: The factories keep on changing the environment, so it works well on your test set.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But guess what? Something changes in the factory. The lights go on and off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Recently, there was a factory in which a bird flew through the factory and pooped on something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That changed stuff. Increasing our algorithmic robustness, all the changes happen in the factory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I find that we run into a lot of practical problems that are not as widely discussed in academia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's really fun being on the cutting edge solving these problems before many people are even aware that there is a problem there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That's such a fascinating space. You're absolutely right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But what is the first step that a company should take? It's just a scary leap into this new world of going from the human eye,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: inspecting to digitizing that process, having a camera, having an algorithm.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: What's the first step? What's the early journey that you recommend that you see these companies taking?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I published a document called the AI Transformation Playbook that's online and taught briefly in the AI for Everyone course on Coursera

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: about the long-term journey that companies should take. But the first step is actually to start small.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I've seen a lot more companies fail by starting too big than by starting too small. Take even Google.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Most people don't realize how hard it was and how controversial it was in the early days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So when I started Google Brain, it was controversial. People thought deep learning, neural nets, tried it, didn't work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Why would you want to do deep learning? So my first internal customer within Google was the Google Speech Team,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: which is not the most lucrative project in Google, not the most important. It's not web search or advertising.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But by starting small, my team helped the speech team build a more accurate speech recognition system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And this caused their peers, other teams, to start to have more faith in deep learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: My second internal customer was the Google Maps team, where we used computer vision to read house numbers

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: from basic street view images to more accurately locate houses within Google Maps to improve the quality of geo data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And it was only after those two successes that I then started the more serious conversation with the Google Ads team.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So there's a ripple effect that you showed that it works in these cases and then it just propagates through the entire company

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: that this thing has a lot of value and use for us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think the early small scale projects, it helps the teams gain faith, but also helps the teams learn what these technologies do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I still remember when our first GPU server, it was a server under some guy's desk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And that taught us early important lessons about how do you have multiple users share a set of GPUs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: which was really not obvious at the time, but those early lessons were important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: We learned a lot from that first GPU server that later helped the teams think through how to scale it up to much larger deployments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Are there concrete challenges that companies face that you see as important for them to solve?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think building and deploying machine learning systems is hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: There's a huge gulf between something that works in a Jupyter notebook on your laptop

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: versus something that runs in a production deployment setting in a factory or agriculture, plant or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I see a lot of people get something to work on your laptop and say, wow, look what I've done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And that's great. That's hard. That's a very important first step.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But a lot of teams underestimate the rest of the steps needed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So for example, I've heard this exact same conversation between a lot of machine learning people and business people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: The machine learning person says, look, my algorithm does well on the test set.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: It's a clean test set. I didn't peek.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And the business person says, thank you very much, but your algorithm sucks. It doesn't work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And the machine learning person says, no, wait, I did well on the test set.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I think there is a gulf between what it takes to do well on a test set on your hard drive

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: versus what it takes to work well in a deployment setting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Some common problems, robustness and generalization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You deploy something in the factory, maybe they chop down a tree outside the factory

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: so the tree no longer covers the window and the lighting is different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So the test set changes. And in machine learning, and especially in academia,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: we don't know how to deal with test set distributions that are dramatically different than the training set distribution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: There's research, there's stuff like domain annotation, transfer learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: There are people working on it, but we're really not good at this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So how do you actually get this to work? Because your test set distribution is going to change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I think also, if you look at the number of lines of code in the software system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: the machine learning model is maybe 5% or even fewer relative to the entire software system you need to build.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So how do you get all that work done and make it reliable and systematic?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So good software engineering work is fundamental here to building a successful small machine learning system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yes. And the software system needs to interface with people's workloads.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So machine learning is automation on steroids. If we take one task out of many tasks that are done in the factory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So the factory does lots of things. One task is visual inspection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: If we automate that one task, it can be really valuable,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: but you may need to redesign a lot of other tasks around that one task.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: For example, say the machine learning algorithm says this is defective. What are you supposed to do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Do you throw it away? Do you get a human to double check? Do you want to rework it or fix it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So you need to redesign a lot of tasks around that thing you've now automated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So planning for the change management and making sure that the software you write is consistent with the new workflow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And you take the time to explain to people what needs to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think what landing AI has become good at, and I think we learned by making the steps and painful experiences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: What we've become good at is working with our partners to think through all the things beyond just the machine learning model

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: that you put in the notebook, but to build the entire system,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: manage the change process and figure out how to deploy this in a way that has an actual impact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: The processes that the large software tech companies use for deploying don't work for a lot of other scenarios.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: For example, when I was leading large speech teams, if the speech recognition system goes down, what happens?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Well, allowance goes off and then someone like me would say, hey, you 20 engineers, please fix this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But if you have a system go down in the factory, there are not 20 machine learning engineers sitting around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You can pay your duty and have them fix it. So how do you deal with the maintenance or the DevOps or the MLops or the other aspects of this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So these are concepts that I think landing AI and a few other teams are in the cutting edge.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But we don't even have systematic terminology yet to describe some of the stuff we do because I think we're inventing it on the fly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So you mentioned some people are interested in discovering mathematical beauty and truth in the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And you're interested in having a big positive impact in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So let me ask. The two are not inconsistent. No, they're all together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I'm only half joking because you're probably interested a little bit in both.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But let me ask a romanticized question. So much of the work, your work and our discussion today has been on applied AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Maybe you can even call narrow AI where the goal is to create systems that automate some specific process that adds a lot of value to the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But there's another branch of AI, starting with Alan Turing, that kind of dreams of creating human level or superhuman level intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Is this something you dream of as well?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Do you think we human beings will ever build a human level intelligence or superhuman level intelligence system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I would love to get to AGI and I think humanity will.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But whether it takes 100 years or 500 or 5000, I find hard to estimate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Do you have some folks have worries about the different trajectories that path would take even existential threats of an AGI system?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Do you have such concerns, whether in the short term or the long term?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I do worry about the long term fate of humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I do wonder as well. I do worry about overpopulation on the planet Mars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Just not today. I think there will be a day when maybe maybe someday in the future, Mars will be polluted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: There are these children dying and someone will look back at this video and say, Andrew, how is that just so hot?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You didn't care about all these children dying on the planet Mars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And I apologize to the future viewer. I do care about the children, but I just don't know how to productively work on that today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Your picture will be in the dictionary for the people who are ignorant about the overpopulation on Mars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yes. So it's a long term problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Is there something in the short term we should be thinking about in terms of aligning the values of our AI systems with the values of us humans?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Sort of something that Stuart Russell and other folks are thinking about as this system develops more and more,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: we want to make sure that it represents the better angels of our nature, the ethics, the values of our society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You know, if you take self-driving cars, the biggest problem with self-driving cars is not that there's some trolley dilemma.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And you teach this. So, you know, how many times when you're driving your car, did you face this moral dilemma?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Who do I crash into? So I think self-driving cars will run into that problem roughly as often as we do when we drive our cars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: The biggest problem with self-driving cars is when there's a big white truck across the road.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And what you should do is brake and not crash into it. And the self-driving car fails and it crashes into it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I think we need to solve that problem first. I think the problem with some of these discussions about AGI, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: alignment, the paperclip problem is that is a huge distraction from the much harder problems that we actually need to address today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Some of the hard problems we need to address today. I think bias is a huge issue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I worry about wealth and equality. The AI and Internet are causing an acceleration of concentration of power

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: because we can now centralize data, use AI to process it. And so industry after industry, we've affected every industry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So the Internet industry has a lot of win-and-take modes of win-and-take-all dynamics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But we've infected all these other industries. So we're also giving these other industries win-and-take-modes of win-and-take-all flavors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So look at what Uber and Lyft did to the taxi industry. So we're doing this type of thing to a lot of industries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So we're creating tremendous wealth, but how do we make sure that the wealth is fairly shared?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think that's... And how do we help people whose jobs are displaced?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think education is part of it. There may be even more that we need to do than education.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think bias is a serious issue. There are adverse uses of AI, like deepfakes being used for various and various purposes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So I worry about some teams maybe accidentally, and I hope not deliberately, making a lot of noise about things that...

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: problems in the distant future rather than focusing on some of the much harder problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah, they overshadow the problems that we have already today. They're exceptionally challenging, like those you said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And even the silly ones, but the ones that have a huge impact, which is the lighting variation outside of your factory window.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: That ultimately is what makes the difference between, like you said, the Jupyter Notebook and something that actually transforms an entire industry potentially.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Yeah. And I think... And just some companies or regulator comes to you and says, look, your product is messing things up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Fixing it may have a revenue impact. Well, it's much more fun to talk to them about how you promise not to wipe out humanity

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: than to face the actually really hard problems we face.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So your life has been a great journey from teaching to research to entrepreneurship. Two questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: One, are there regrets, moments that if you went back, you would do differently?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And two, are there moments you're especially proud of, moments that made you truly happy?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: You know, I've made so many mistakes. It feels like every time I discover something, I go, why didn't I think of this, you know, five years earlier or even 10 years earlier?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And sometimes I read a book and I go, I wish I read this book 10 years ago. My life would have been so different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Although that happened recently. And then I was thinking, if only I read this book when we're starting up Coursera, it could have been so much better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But I discovered the book had not yet been written. We're starting Coursera. So that made me feel better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But I find that the process of discovery, we keep on finding out things that seem so obvious in hindsight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: But it always takes us so much longer than I wish to figure it out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So on the second question, are there moments in your life that if you look back that you're especially proud of or you're especially happy, that filled you with happiness and fulfillment?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Well, two answers. One, does my daughter know about? Yes, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Because I know how much time I spend with her. I just can't spend enough time with her. Congratulations, by the way. Thank you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And then second is helping other people. I think to me, I think the meaning of life is helping others achieve whatever are their dreams.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And then also to try to move the world forward by making humanity more powerful as a whole.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: So the times that I felt most happy, most proud was when I felt someone else allowed me the good fortune of helping them a little bit on the path to their dreams.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: I think there's no better way to end it than talking about happiness and the meaning of life. So Andrew, it's a huge honor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Me and millions of people, thank you for all the work you've done. Thank you for talking today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Thank you so much. Thanks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: And now let me leave you with some words of wisdom from Andrew Ng.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Ask yourself if what you're working on succeeds beyond your wildest dreams, which have significantly helped other people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: If not, then keep searching for something else to work on. Otherwise, you're not living up to your full potential.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrew Ng: Deep Learning, Education, and Real-World AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #73

body.input: Thank you for listening and hope to see you next time.

body.input: The following is a conversation with Andrei Kapothe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: He is one of the greatest scientists, engineers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: and educators in the history of artificial intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: And now, dear friends, here's Andrei Kapothe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: What is a neural network?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: And why does it seem to do such a surprisingly good job

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: of learning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: What is a neural network?

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: It's a mathematical abstraction of the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: I would say that's how it was originally developed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: At the end of the day, it's a mathematical expression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: And it's a fairly simple mathematical expression

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: when you get down to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: It's basically a sequence of matrix multiplies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: which are really dot products mathematically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: and some nonlinearity is thrown in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: And so it's a very simple mathematical expression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: And it's got knobs in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: Many knobs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: Many knobs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: And these knobs are loosely related to basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: the synapses in your brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: They're trainable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: They're modifiable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: And so the idea is we need to find the setting of the knobs

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: that makes the neural net do whatever you want it to do,

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: like classify images and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: And so there's not too much mystery, I would say, in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: You might think that basically you

metadata.title: Podcast: Andrej Karpathy: Tesla AI, Self-Driving, Optimus, Aliens, and AGI | Lex Fridman Podcast #333

body.input: don't want to endow it with too much meaning with respect

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: eating some delicious Texas barbecue, talking about life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: about music, about art, about beauty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: This was a conversation and experience I'll never forget.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: This is the Lex Friedman podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: To support it, please check out our sponsors

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: And now, dear friends, here's Rick Rubin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Are you nervous?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: I'm not shaky, but I would say I feel uneasy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: And I feel like the sooner we start talking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: the more relaxed we'll get.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Well, maybe we should sit in this moment

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: and enjoy the nervousness of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Let me start with Nietzsche.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: He said, without music, life would be a mistake.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: What do you think he means by that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Let's talk some philosophy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Let's try to analyze Friedrich Nietzsche from a century ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: It seems like music has the ability

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: to bring us so much depth in our soul

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: that's hard to access any other way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: And without it, there would be a loss,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: beyond the pleasure of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: It feels like it's a window into something else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Something that no other medium can express

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: quite the same way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: I would say not as automatically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Something about music can do it automatically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Maybe poetry or maybe certain abstract forms

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: can get us there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: But there's something about music

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: that really can get us there quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: But it's also the time, the place, the history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: There's something about, a lot of my family's still in Philly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: There's something about driving through Jersey

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: and listening to Bruce Springsteen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: And then you just, I'll get emotional.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Like listening to I'm on Fire.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: One of my favorite Bruce Springsteen songs,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: there's a haunting kind of strumming to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: It's not a strumming, it's actually picked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: It has a country feel to it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: almost like a Johnny Cash feel actually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: And it, I don't know, makes me feel,

body.input: so for people who don't know I'm on Fire,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: that song is, I guess, a love song to a woman

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: that you can't have because she's married

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: or she's with somebody else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Which I guess is quite a lot of love songs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: But there's something about the haunting nature

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: of the guitar and then it has to be driving through Jersey.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: And I feel like everyone has fallen in love

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: with a Jersey girl at one point in their life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: I don't know if that's true for her,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: but I feel like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: I haven't either, but I just feel like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: There's something about Bruce Springsteen

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: is like, yeah, I've been there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: And that just takes you to a place of emotion

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: that you just, that captures love,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: that captures longing, that captures the heartbreak

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: of just the way time flows in life

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: and the fact that it's finite.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: And just all of that in a single, simple song.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: What else can capture that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Yeah, I don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: But it's true that there's a connection

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: both between time and place and music.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: all of a sudden the music of the Eagles

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: felt appropriate somehow.

body.input: What other places have a sound in the United States?

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: And that said, sometimes we can get an experience

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: through music of a place.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: You can just listen to Texas Flood and just,

body.input: again, there's this like a woman you're missing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: And I've lived with that song for a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: but there's also the soulfulness of the lyrics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: which I still don't understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: And it could be about anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: And as you get older,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: Yeah, I think that's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: I think that's the beauty of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

body.input: I think when the person wrote them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275

metadata.title: Podcast: Rick Rubin: Legendary Music Producer | Lex Fridman Podcast #275
