body.input: Satra, he declined the Nobel prizes we discussed, but he also was mocking people that pretend to be something better than they are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: He was living an authentic life that is sincere. And that's what appealed to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And Albert Camus was another French philosopher that advocated existentialism. That really appealed to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: That's probably my favorite existentialist, Camus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Yeah. And he died at a young age in an accident, unfortunately.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And then people like Nietzsche broke conventions. And I noticed that Nietzsche is still extremely popular.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: That's quite surprising. He appeals to the young people of today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: It's the childlike wonder about the world. And he was unapologetic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Most philosophers have a very strict adherence to terminology and to the practices of academic philosophers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And Nietzsche was full of contradictions. And he was just this big kid with opinions and thought deeply about this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And people are really attracted to that. And surprisingly, there's not enough people like that throughout history of philosophy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And that's why I think he's still drawn to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Yeah. To me, what stands out is his statement that the best way to corrupt the mind of young people is to tell them that they should agree with the common view.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And it goes back to the thread that went throughout discussion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Yes. You've kind of suggested that we ought to be humble about our very own existence and that our existence lasts only a short time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: We talked about you losing your father and your mother. Do you think about your own mortality? Are you afraid of death?

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: I'm not afraid. You know what? Epicorus was a very wise person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: According to Lucretius, Epicorus didn't leave anything in writing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: But he said that he's never afraid of death because as long as he's around, death is not around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And when death will be around, he will not be around. So he will never meet death.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: So why should you be worried about something you will never meet?

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And it's an interesting philosophy of life. You shouldn't be afraid of something that you will never encounter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: But there's a finiteness to this experience. We live every day. I think, if we're being honest, we live every day as if it's going to last forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: We often kind of don't contemplate the fact that it ends. You kind of have plans and goals and you have these possibilities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: You have a kind of lingering thought, especially as you get older and older and older, that this is, especially when you lose friends, then you start to realize it doesn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: But I don't know if you really are cognizant of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: But you have to be careful not to be depressed by it because otherwise you lose the vitality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: So I think the most important thing to draw from knowing that you are short-lived is a sense of appreciation that you are alive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: That's the first thing. But more importantly, a sense of modesty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Because how can anyone be arrogant if they kept at the same time this notion that they are short-lived?

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: I mean, you cannot be arrogant because anything that you advocate for, you will not be around to do that in 100 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: So people will just forget and move on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And if you keep that in mind, the Caesars in ancient Rome, they had a person next to them telling them, don't forget that you're mortal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: There was a person with that duty because the Caesars thought that they are all powerful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And they had, for a good reason, someone they hired to whisper in their ear, don't forget that you're mortal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Well, you're one of the most respected famous scientists in the world sitting on a farm, gazing up at the stars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: So you seem like an appropriate person to ask the completely inappropriate question of what do you think is the meaning of it all?

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: What's the meaning of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: That's an excellent question. And if we ever find an alien that we can converse with, I would like to ask for an answer to this question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Would they have a different opinion, you think?

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Well, they might be wiser because they lived around for a while, but I'm afraid they will be silent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: I'm afraid they will not have a good answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And I think it's the process that you should get satisfied by, the process of learning you should enjoy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Okay, so it's not so much that there is a meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: In fact, there is, as far as I can tell, things just exist.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And I think it's inappropriate for us to assign meaning for our existence because as a civilization, we will eventually perish.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And nothing will be, just another planet on which life died.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And if you look at the big scheme of things, who cares?

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And how can we assign significance to what we are doing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: So if you said the meaning of life is this, well, it will not be around in a billion years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: So it cannot be the meaning of life because nothing will be around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: So I think we should just enjoy the process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And it's like many other things in life. You enjoy good food.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And you can enjoy learning. Why? Because it makes you appreciate better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: The environment that you live in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And sometimes people think religion, for example, is in conflict with science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Spirituality. That's not true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: If you see a watch and you look at it from the outside, you might say, oh, that's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: But then if you start to open it up and learn about how it works, you appreciate it more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: So science is the way to learn about how the world works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And it's not in conflict to the meaning that you assign to all of this, but it helps you appreciate the world better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: So in fact, I would think that a religious person should promote science because it gives you a better appreciation of what's around you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: It's like if you buy in a grocery, buy something, a bunch of fruits that are packed together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: and you can't see from the outside exactly what kind of fruits are inside.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: But if you open it up and study, you appreciate better the merchandise that you get.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: So you pay the same amount of money, but at least you know what's inside.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: So why don't we figure out what the world is about? What the universe contains? What is the dark matter?

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: It will help us appreciate the bigger picture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And then you can assign your own flavor to what it means.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: I think I'm truly grateful that a person like you exists at the center of the scientific community.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: It gives me faith and hope about this big journey that we call science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: So thank you for writing the book you wrote recently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: You have many other books and articles that I think people should definitely read.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: And thank you for wasting all this time with me. It is truly an honor. Thank you so much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: It was not a waste at all. And thank you for having me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: I learned a lot from your questions and your remarks. Thank you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Thank you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Thanks for listening to this conversation with Avi Loeb.

body.input: And now let me leave you with some words from Albert Einstein.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: The important thing is not to stop questioning. Curiosity has its own reason for existence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua | Lex Fridman Podcast #154

body.input: Also, if you for instance look, if you train agent in 3D world,

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah, I thought that that's what you are referring to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Well, I was referring more on not an actual voice.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I meant like there's some kind of subjective experience feels like it's fundamentally about storytelling to ourselves.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So there feels like it's a very high level abstraction that is useful for me to feel like entity in this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Most useful aspect of it is that because I'm conscious,

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I think there's an intricate connection to me not wanting to die.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So like it's a useful hack to really prioritize not dying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Those seem to be somewhat connected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So I'm telling the story of like it's rich.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Feels like something to be me and the fact that me exists in this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I want to preserve me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So that makes it a useful agent hack.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So I will just refer maybe to that first part, as you said, about that kind of story of describing who you are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I was thinking about it even.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Obviously, I like thinking about consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I like thinking about AI as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And I'm trying to see analogies of these things in AI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: What would it correspond to?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So OpenAI trained a model called GPT, which can generate pretty amusing text on arbitrary topic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And one way to control GPT is by putting into prefix at the beginning of the text some information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: What would be the story about?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: You can have even chat with GPT by saying that the chat is with Lex or Elon Musk or so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And GPT would just pretend to be you or Elon Musk or so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And it almost feels that this story that we give ourselves to describe our life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: it's almost like things that you put into context of GPT.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah, but the context we provide to GPT is multimodal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So GPT itself is multimodal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: GPT itself hasn't learned actually from experience of single human, but from the experience of humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It's a chameleon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: You can turn it into anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And in some sense, by providing context, it behaves as the thing that you wanted it to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It's interesting that people have stories of who they are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And as I said, these stories, they help them to operate in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: But it's also interesting, I guess, various people find it out through meditation or so that there might be some patterns that you have learned when you were a kid that actually are not serving you anymore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And you also might be thinking that that's who you are. And that's actually just a story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yes, it's a useful hack, but sometimes it gets us into trouble.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It's a local optima. It's a local optima.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: You wrote that Stephen Hawking, he tweeted, Stephen Hawking asked what breathes fire into equations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: which meant what makes given mathematical equations realize the physics of a universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Similarly, I wonder what breathes fire into computation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: What makes given computation conscious?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: OK, so how do we engineer consciousness?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: How do you breathe fire and magic into the machine?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So it seems clear to me that not every computation is conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I mean, you can, let's say, just keep on multiplying one matrix over and over again and maybe gigantic matrix.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: You can put a lot of computation. I don't think it would be conscious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So in some sense, the question is, what are the computations which could be conscious?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I mean, so one assumption is that it has to do purely with computation, that you can abstract away matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Other possibilities that it's very important was the realization of computation that it has to do with some force fields or so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And they bring consciousness. At the moment, my intuition is that it can be fully abstracted away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So in case of computation, you can ask yourself, what are the mathematical objects or so that could bring such properties?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So for instance, if we think about the models, AI models, what they truly try to do, or like models like GPT,

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: is they try to predict next word or so. And this turns out to be equivalent to compressing text.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And because in some sense, compression means that you learn the model of reality and you have just to remember where are your mistakes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: The better you are in predicting. And in some sense, when we look at our experience, also when you look, for instance, at the car driving,

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: you know in which direction it will go. You are good in prediction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And it might be the case that the consciousness is intertwined with compression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It might be also the case that self-consciousness has to do with compressor trying to compress itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So I was just wondering what are the objects in mathematics or computer science, which are mysterious,

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: that could have to do with consciousness. And then I thought, you see in mathematics, there is something called Gadel theorem,

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: which means if you have sufficiently complicated mathematical system, it is possible to point the mathematical system back on itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: In computer science, there is something called halting problem. It's somewhat similar construction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So I thought that if we believe that under assumption that consciousness has to do with compression,

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: then you could imagine that as you keep on compressing things, then at some point it actually makes sense for the compressor to compress itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Metacompression. Consciousness is metacompression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: That's an idea. And in some sense, you know, the crazy...

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Thank you. But do you think if we think of a touring machine, a universal touring machine, can that achieve consciousness?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So is there something beyond our traditional definition of computation that's required?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So it's a specific computation. And I said this computation has to do with compression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And the compression itself, maybe other way of putting it is like you are internally creating the model of reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: In order that you try inside to simplify reality in order to predict what's going to happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And that also feels somewhat similar to how I think actually about my own conscious experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So clearly I don't have access to reality. The only access to reality is through, you know, cable going to my brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And my brain is creating a simulation of reality and I have access to the simulation of reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Are you by any chance aware of the Hutter Prize, Marcus Hutter?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: He made this prize for compression of Wikipedia pages. And there's a few qualities to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: One, I think, has to be perfect compression, which makes...

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I think that little quirk makes it much less applicable to the general task of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Because it feels like intelligence is always going to be messy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Like perfect compression feels like it's not the right goal, but it's nevertheless a very interesting goal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So for him, intelligence equals compression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And so the smaller you make the file, given a large Wikipedia page, the more intelligent the system has to be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah, that makes sense. So you can make perfect compression if you store errors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And I think that actually what he meant is you have algorithm plus errors.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: By the way, Hutter is a... he was a PhD advisor of Chen Leck, who is a DeepMind co-founder.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah, yeah. So there's an interesting... and now he's a DeepMind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: There's an interesting network of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: He's one of the people that I think seriously took on the task of what would an AGI system look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I think for the longest time, the question of AGI was not taken seriously or rather rigorously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And he did just that. Like mathematically speaking, what would the model look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: If you remove the constraints of it having to be... having to have a reasonable amount of memory,

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: reasonable amount of running time complexity, computation time, what would it look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And essentially, it's a half math, half philosophical discussion of how would a reinforcement learning type of framework look like for an AGI?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So he developed the framework even to describe what's optimal with respect to reinforcement learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Like there is a theoretical framework, which is, as you said, under assumption, there is infinite amount of memory and compute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So that's the task. And you could imagine that every task could be casted as such a task.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So let's say you read already n bits and you want to predict n plus 1 bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So you read n bits, you enumerate all the programs that produce these n bits in their output.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And then in order to predict n plus 1 bit, you actually weight the programs according to their length.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And then the n plus 1 bit prediction is the prediction from each of these programs according to that weight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Like statistically. So the smaller the program, the more likely you are to pick its output.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And it will be a matter of there will be algorithms that vastly decrease sample complexity. I believe so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: But the place where we are heading today is there are domains which contains million X more data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And even though computers might be 1000 times slower than humans in learning, that's not the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: For instance, I believe that it should be possible to create superhuman therapies by and there are even simple steps of doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And, you know, that the core reason is there is just machine will be able to read way more transcripts of therapies and then it should be able to speak simultaneously with many more people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And it should be possible to optimize it all in parallel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Well, there's now you're touching on something I deeply care about and think is way harder than we imagine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: What's the goal of a therapist? What's the goal of therapists?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So, OK, so one goal. Now, this is terrifying to me, but there's a lot of people that contemplate suicide, suffer from depression, and they could significantly be helped with therapy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And the idea that an AI algorithm might be in charge of that, it's like a life and death task.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It's the stakes are high. So one goal for a therapist, whether human or AI, is to prevent suicide ideation to prevent suicide.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: How do you achieve that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So let's see. So to be clear, I don't think that the current models are good enough for such a task because it requires insane amount of understanding and patting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And the models are far from this place. But it's.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: But do you think that understanding empathy, that signal is in the data?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I think there is some signal in the data. Yes. I mean, there are plenty of transcripts of conversations and it is possible to it is possible from it to understand personalities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It is possible from it to understand if conversation is friendly, amicable, antagonistic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It is, I believe that, you know, given the fact that the models that we train now, they can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: They can have they are chameleons that they can have any personality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: They might turn out to be better in understanding personality of other people than anyone else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And they are pathetic to be empathetic. Yeah. Interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: But I wonder if there's some level of multiple modalities required to be able to be empathetic of the human experience, whether language is not enough to understand death, to understand fear, to understand childhood trauma,

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: to understand wit and humor required when you're dancing with a person who might be depressed or suffering, both humor and hope and love and all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So there's another underlying question, which is self supervised versus supervised.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So can you get that from the data by just reading a huge number of transcripts? I actually so I think that reading huge number of transcripts is a step one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It's like the same way as you cannot learn to dance if just from YouTube by watching it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: You have to actually try it out yourself. And so I think that here that's a similar situation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I also wouldn't deploy the system in the high stakes situations right away, but kind of see gradually where it goes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And obviously, initially, it would have to go hand in hand with humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: But at the moment, we are in the situation that actually there is many more people who actually would like to have a therapy or speak with someone than there are therapies out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I can you know, I was so fundamentally, I was thinking, what are the things that can vastly increase people well-being?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Therapy is one of them. Being meditation is other one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I guess maybe human connection is the third one. And I guess pharmacologically, it's also possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Maybe direct brain stimulation or something like that. But these are pretty much options out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Then let's say the way I'm thinking about the AGI endeavor is by default, that's an endeavor to increase the amount of wealth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And I believe that we can vastly increase the amount of wealth for everyone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And simultaneously, so I mean, there are like two endeavors that make sense to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: One is like essentially increase the amount of wealth. And the second one is increase overall human well-being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And those are coupled together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I would say these are different topics. One can help another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And you know, therapist is a funny word because I see friendship and love as therapy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I mean, so therapist broadly defined is just friendship as a friend.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So like therapist has a very kind of clinical sense to it. But what is human connection?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: You're like not to get all Camus and Dostoevsky on you, but you know, life is suffering and we draw.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: We seek connection with other humans as we desperately try to make sense of this world in a deep, overwhelming loneliness that we feel inside.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So I think connection has to do with understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And I think that almost like a lack of understanding causes suffering. If you speak with someone and you feel ignored, that actually causes pain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: If you are feeling deeply understood that actually they might not even tell you what to do in life, but like a pure understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Or just being heard. Understanding is a kind of, it's a lot, you know, just being heard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Feel like you're being heard. Like somehow that's alleviation temporarily of the loneliness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: That if somebody knows you're here with their body language, with the way they are, with the way they look at you, with the way they talk, you feel less alone for a brief moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah, very much agree. So I thought in the past about somewhat similar question to yours, which is what is love rather what is connection?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And obviously I think about these things from AI perspective. What would it mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So I said that intelligence has to do with some compression, which is more or less like you can say almost understanding of what is going around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It seems to me that other aspect is there seem to be reward functions and you can have a reward for food, for maybe human connection, for let's say warmth, sex, and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And it turns out that the various people might be optimizing slightly different reward functions. They essentially might care about different things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And in case of love, at least the love between two people, you can say that the boundary between people dissolves to such extent that they end up optimizing each other reward functions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah, that's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Celebrate the success of each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah, in some sense, I would say love means helping others to optimize their reward functions, not your reward functions, not the things that you think are important, but the things that the person cares about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: You try to help them to optimize it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So love is, if you think of two reward functions, you just it's a condition. You combine them together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah, pretty much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Maybe like with a weight and it depends like the dynamic of the relationship.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah, I mean, you could imagine that if you are fully optimizing someone's reward function without yours, then maybe you are creating codependency or something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I'm not sure what's the appropriate weight. But the interesting thing is I even think that the individual person, we ourselves, we are actually less of a unified insight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So, for instance, if you look at the donut on the one level, you might think, oh, this looks tasty. I would like to eat it. On the other level, you might tell yourself, I shouldn't be doing it because I want to gain muscles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So and you know, you might do it regardless, kind of against yourself. So it seems that even within ourselves, they're almost like a kind of intertwined personas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And I believe that the self love means that the love between all these personas, which also means being able to love yourself when you are angry or stressed or so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Combining all those reward functions of the different selves you have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah, and accepting that they are there. Like, you know, often people, they have a negative self-talk or they say, I don't like when I'm angry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And like I tried to imagine, tried to imagine if there would be like a small baby Lex, like a five years old, angry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And then they are like, you shouldn't be angry. Like, stop being angry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah. But like instead, actually, you want the Lex to come over, give him a hug and is like, I say, it's fine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: OK, you can be angry as long as you want. And then he would stop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Or maybe not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Or maybe not. But you cannot expect it even.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah. But still, that doesn't explain the why of love. Like, why is love part of the human condition?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Why is it useful to combine the reward functions?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It seems like that doesn't I mean, I don't think reinforcement learning frameworks can give us answers to why even even the Hutter framework has an objective function that's static.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So we came to existence as a consequence of evolutionary process.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And in some sense, the purpose of evolution is survival.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And then this complicated optimization objective baked into us, let's say compression, which might help us operate in the real world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And it baked into us various reward functions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Then to be clear, at the moment, we are operating in the regime, which is somewhat out of distribution where the even evolution optimized us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It's almost like love is a consequence of cooperation that we've discovered is useful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Correct. In some way, it's even the case if you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I just love the idea that love is like the out of distribution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Or it's not out of distribution. It's like as you said, it evolved for cooperation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And I believe that the cop like in some sense, cooperation ends up helping each of us individually.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So it makes sense evolutionary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And there is in some sense, and you know, love means there is this dissolution of boundaries that you have a shared reward function.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And we evolved to actually identify ourselves with larger groups.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So we can identify ourselves with a family.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: We can identify ourselves with a country to such extent that people are willing to give away their life for country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So there is we are wired, actually, even for love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And at the moment, I guess the maybe it would be somewhat more beneficial if you will, if we would identify ourselves with all the humanity as a whole.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So you can clearly see when people travel around the world, when they run into person from the same country, they say, oh, which city are and all this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Like all the sudden they find all these similarities. They they they find some they befriended those folks earlier than others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So there is like a sense, some sense of the belonging.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And I would say I think it would be overall good thing to the world for people to move towards.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: I think it's even called open individualism, move toward the mindset of a larger and larger groups.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So the challenge there, that's a beautiful vision. And I share it to expand that circle of empathy, that circle of love towards the entirety of humanity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: But then you start to ask, well, where do you draw the line? Because why not expand it to other conscious beings?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And then finally, for our discussion, something I think about is why not expand it to AI systems?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Like we we start respecting each other when the person, the entity on the other side has the capacity to suffer, because then we develop a capacity to sort of empathize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And so I could see AI systems that are interacting with humans more and more having conscious like displays.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So like they display consciousness through language and through other means.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It makes you realize like, yeah, the limits that the human intellect might be limitless. I was just impressive to see a descendant of APE come up with clever ideas.

And if someone invented it multiple times, you know, if a probability of inventing it once is one over a million, then probability of inventing it twice or three times would be one over a million square or to the power of three, which would be just impossible.

body.input: It also feels that, for instance, if you think about folks like Gauss or Euler, you know, at first they read a lot of books, and then they did thinking, and then they figure out math.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: He makes me realize that there's like deep thinking that the human mind can do. Like most of us are not thinking deeply. Like you really have to put a lot of effort to think deeply.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: But I mean, Cal Newport talks about this as ideas of deep work. It's you know, most of us don't work much at all in terms of like like deeply think about particular problems, whether it's a math, engineering, all that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Before I go on to that thread, let me return to our friend GPT.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Let me ask you another ridiculously big question. Can you give an overview of what GPT-3 is or like you say in your Twitter bio, GPT N plus one, how it works and why it works?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So GPT-3 is a human-goose neural network. Let's assume that we know what is neural network by definition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And it is trained on the entire Internet just to predict next words. So let's say it sees part of the article and the only task that it has at hand is to say what would be the next word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: What would be the next word? And it becomes really exceptional at the task of figuring out what's the next word.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So you might ask, why would this be an important task? Why would it be important to predict what's the next word?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And it turns out that a lot of problems can be formulated as a text completion problem. So GPT is purely learning to complete the text.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: You could imagine, for instance, if you are asking a question, who is the president of the United States, then GPT can give you an answer to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It turns out that many more things can be formulated this way. You can format text in the way that you have sent us in English.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: You make it even look like some content of a website elsewhere, which would be teaching people how to translate things between languages. So it would be EN colon, text in English, FR colon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And then you ask the model to continue. And it turns out that such a model is predicting translation from English to French.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: The crazy thing is that this model can be used for way more sophisticated tasks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So you can format text such that it looks like a conversation between two people. And that might be a conversation between you and Elon Musk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And because the model read all the text about Elon Musk, it will be able to predict Elon Musk words as it would be Elon Musk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It will speak about colonization of Mars, about sustainable future and so on. And it's also possible to even give arbitrary personality to the model.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: You can say, here is a conversation with a friendly AI bot. And the model will complete the text as a friendly AI bot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So, I mean, how do I express how amazing this is? So just to clarify a conversation, generating a conversation between me and Elon Musk, it wouldn't just generate good examples of what Elon would say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It would get the syntax all correct. So like interview style, it would say like Elon colon and Lex colon. It's not just like inklings of semantic correctness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: It's like the whole thing. Grammatical, syntactic, semantic. It's just really, really impressive generalization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: Yeah, I mean, I also want to provide some caveats. So it can generate a few paragraphs of coherent text.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: But as you go to longer pieces, it actually goes off the rails. If you try to write a book, it won't work out this way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: What way does it go off the rails, by the way? Is there interesting ways in which it goes off the rails? What falls apart first?

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So the model is trained on all the existing data that is out there, which means that it is not trained on its own mistakes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: So, for instance, if it would make a mistake, then I can give you an example.

body.input: So let's say I have a conversation with a model pretending that is Elon Musk. And then I start putting some, I start actually making up things which are not factual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Wojciech Zaremba: OpenAI Codex, GPT-3, Robotics, and the Future of AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #215

body.input: And it's also interesting. I mean, first of all, humans have the same problem is just that we will make fewer errors and magnify the errors slower.
